# `lss.map.md` — architecture & navigation map for `index-working.html`

> Companion map to the WebGL game in `LSS/`. Current as of build **v47.26**.
>
> ⚠ **This maps `index-working.html`, the commented SOURCE you edit** — NOT `index.html`, which since the dual-file split is a ~6.7k-line shell that loads the generated `lss.js`. Run `python strip.py` from the repo root to regenerate; see [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).
>
> The game is **one classic `<script>`** defining `function _bootLSS()` — one giant shared lexical scope, no modules. It spans essentially the whole file (from ~L6.8k to the end of ~143k source lines; 4 → ~96k in the generated `lss.js`), which is why almost nothing is reachable from the console: use the `window.__*` probes instead.
>
> ⚠ **These figures drift, and this header was stale for a long time** — it claimed build v36.56 and "lines 3036–70463" well after both were wrong, and still described the pre-split single file. **Re-derive rather than trust it:** `grep -n 'function _bootLSS' index-working.html`, `wc -l`, and `grep LSS_BUILD`. The same applies to every `~L#####` hint below — jump by the `Jump:` anchor, which never drifts.

## How to use this file

- **New here? Read [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) first.** It is the short version: how Ashman and you actually work together, the two-file build (`index-working.html` -> `strip.py`), the rules that bite on the FIRST action (UTF-8, TDZ, `LSS_BUILD`, backups), and how to run and measure. **This file is the long version** - the architecture map and the trap log. CLAUDE.md loads automatically; this one you open.

- **Jump by anchor, not by line number.** Each entry has a **`Jump:`** string — a unique declaration you can Ctrl-F / grep for (`function fireWeapon`, `class Bot`, `const audio`). The `~L#####` line hints are approximate and **drift** as the file grows; the anchor never does.
- **To find a subsystem:** scan the Section Map below (it's in file order, grouped into PARTs), grab the `Jump:` anchor, search for it in `index.html`.
- **To keep this current:** when you add/remove/rename a subsystem, update its entry here. Keep entries **coarse** (subsystem-level, not per-function). To refresh the `~L` hints after big edits, grep each anchor.
- **Sibling of** `index.html` in `LSS/` — the **site root** since v36.09: `LSS/` is exactly what deploys to `lss.fractalreality.ca` (via `tools/deploy_cf.py`); the repo root above it holds only dev tooling (`strip.py`, `check_scripts.js`, `tools/`) and separate projects, none of which ship. This is a doc — it changes nothing at runtime and preserves the single-file build.
- **(v47.03) `window.__demReport()` — the EARTH DEM STAGE SPLIT.** `_fetchDemRing` profiles as one 17.9 s blob because the JS self-profiler attributes a FUNCTION, not a statement, so it now carries stage timers (`stats.demMs`: net / decode / fill / hist / wet, and wet splits into close / blur) summed across every `LSSEarthTiles` a launch builds - a near patch AND a far patch, each its own instance. **It immediately killed a plan:** the per-texel height decode everyone assumes is the cost is **7%** (269 ms); the blur was **45%** (1,734 ms) and the float-keyed `Map` histogram **18%** (683 ms). v47.04 took those to 826 / 301 ms. ⚠ Every DEM loop is sliced behind `_leSlicer`, so saving CPU there buys main-thread headroom, NOT curtain time, on a warm-network launch. See [`performance_review.md`](performance_review.md).
- **(v47.05-47.07) TWO IN-PLAY GEOMETRY GATES, AND THE PANE-SIZE TRAP THEY PROVE.** `_swTreeVisTick` hides foliage InstancedMeshes past `uTreeFadeB` (the shader already collapses them to degenerate triangles - zero pixels, FULL vertex cost - and the shadow pass has no fade at all, so it submits them at full size); `_clipSkyOccluder` hides clipmap rings that lie entirely outside the opaque camera-centred sky dome (`renderOrder` 3 vs the rings' -2, so the dome paints over them). Together at 1920x1080: **-2.8 M triangles and -47 draw calls a frame, roughly +14 fps.** ⚠⚠ **THE SAME TREE PATCH MEASURES +0.0 fps AT PANE SIZE AND +4.6% AT 1080p.** Interleave the A/B (`window.__treeVisCull`, `window.__clipCull`) on a SETTLED world - the world streams for minutes after spawn and a sequential before/after is worthless - and make sure any debug toggle RESTORES rather than merely stopping (a non-symmetric off-switch measured the same scene twice). ⚠ `_clipWireParents` points each level's atlas at the NEXT level's texture, so a hidden level's atlas is still sampled: hide `L.mesh` only, NEVER skip `_clipBakeLevel`/`_clipBakeEdge`. See [`performance_review.md`](performance_review.md).
- **(v47.08) `window.__clipReport()` — AND THE HITCH THAT WAS NOT ONE.** Hit/miss counters in `_clipCellH` plus per-level bake timers. A bake texel is an array read when it hits the baked height table and a full `_stGroundYCarved` when it misses (FIVE of them on levels >= `_CLIP_PEAK.minLevel`). Flying the hub at 1400 u/s looked damning - 118 snaps, 2,054 ms, worst 28-40 ms each, `hub:clip` the top frame-spike contributor - **but the misses all start past |x| ~ 45,000, and `_HB_BOX = 53248` is commented "45,056 (cities) + 8,192 (L0 half window)": the flight had gone 31% PAST the world the table is sized for.** Re-flown as a 40,000-radius orbit inside the city ring: **100% hits over 4.43 M samples, 0 misses, 177 ms of bake for MORE bakes (3,184 vs 1,855), L3-L5 avg 0.1 ms instead of 6.7-9.1.** No change made; `_HB_BOX`'s sizing is now measured rather than asserted. ⚠ Open: nothing here checks whether a player can actually fly past +/-45,056 - if they can, the cheap fix is a far table at `sp = 32` (L0 is the ONLY clipmap spacing without one), not a bigger base box.
- **(v47.10) RACE GATES: TWO PATHS INSTALL A CIRCUIT, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM HANDED OVER THE OLD MESHES.** `_raceCircuitAdopt` (the net path) ends with `_raceCircuitInstall(); _raceCircuitOnArrive();` - and `_raceCircuitOnArrive` is what destroys the live `RaceRing`s so gameLoop rebuilds them against the new list. `_raceCircuitTrackBuild` (called from `buildRoomGraphLevel`, i.e. on EVERY round rebuild) assigned `game.raceCircuit = C` and called `_raceCircuitInstall()` **without** `_raceCircuitOnArrive()`. Track circuits re-roll per round with a DIFFERENT gate count (measured on `race_shifting`: round 1 = 12 gates, round 2 = 14), and gameLoop only respawns the meshes `if (!game.poleRings.length)` - so round 2 drew round 1's 12 rings at round 1's positions while the HUD, the minimap and the BOTS all read `C.rings`. Owner: *"i couldn't see the first check point, i saw it on the mini map, and the bots got it and moved on"*. **The tell is `__race.info()`: `rings` != `poleRings`.** Fixed at the source, plus a belt in gameLoop that respawns on a count mismatch and logs `[race] gate desync`. ⚠ Any future path that swaps `game.raceCircuit` must call `_raceCircuitOnArrive()`. **⚠⚠ (v47.84) CORRECTION: that rule is for the NET/DECREE paths only. From INSIDE a level build, call `_raceCircuitHandOver()` (meshes + progress, no placement)** — this fix's `_raceCircuitOnArrive()` also ran `_raceCircuitPlaceAll()` before the build had sampled any spawn points, and that put the pilot at the world origin in every round 2+ of Pole Position and the Shifting Run. See *v47.84* at the end of this file.
- **(v47.11-47.13) THE EARTH WORLD IS KEPT ACROSS A ROUND — `_lssGmapsLevelSig` + `_keepTiles`.** `_lssGmapsBuildLevel` runs on EVERY level build, and a race circuit re-rolls its gates every round, so round 2 used to tear the whole city down (`LSSEarthTiles.dispose()` — **1,692 material disposes**, caught by hooking `Material.prototype.dispose`) and rebuild it from the DEM even though the LOCATION had not moved. JS self-profile over the transition: `boxAny` (the R=8 water-mask closing) **1,740 ms of SELF time**, scene traverse 1,405, getImageData 602, `_fetchDemRing` 519 self / 2,442 total, `_loadBuildingsBody` 1,539, `updateNight` 1,505 — ~5 s of main-thread JS landing as **33 frames over 60 ms, worst 401 ms**. Owner: *"couple hitches in race/earth circuit"*. Same shape as v38.99's `_keepTerrain`: if the signature (streamed-vs-single class, lat/lng, extent, scale, cyberpunk, ads) is unchanged, reuse the world; gates, spawn points and the rest of the build still re-roll. **Measured after: 33 spikes -> 1, worst 401 -> 101 ms, median 8.9, p99 17.1.** `window.__earthKeep = false` for an A/B. ⚠ Keep `_lssGmapsLevelSig` in step with the constructor arguments — a field the constructor reads and the signature does not is a stale world. A typed DROP changes `level.lat/lng` BEFORE the build call, so it correctly rebuilds. **v47.11 also gave that teardown `_lssRetainMat`** (it was the one rebuild the v38.97 program-retention fix never covered: `freed x19`, programs 187->176, then `lambert [RELINK]` and friends). That was real but NOT the main cost — worth knowing, because fixing it alone moved the hitches by nothing.
- **(v47.14) THE EARTH GROUND LIFT — dim the sky without crushing the terrain (`_leApplyGroundLift`).** Owner: *"the ground in the cities [is] very dark, on Earth... the hill is just all black ... we dim the skies in cities to make the cyberpunk buildings look cooler, but maybe there could be a way it doesn't affect the ground so much"*. **MEASURED in Hong Kong:** the earth night rig (`_lssEarthApplyDayNight` -> `_HUB_ZONES.DUSK`) leaves the terrain lit by `AmbientLight 3.73 @ #2b3b90` - a dim BLUE - with key 0.327 / fill 0.151 / rim 0.112 / hemi 0.4, under ACES at exposure 0.78. The TOWERS survive it because their window texels clear the dusk bloom threshold (0.14, strength 1.70) and bloom; bare hillside has no bright texels, so it renders near-black. ⚠ **The facades are `MeshLambertMaterial` with `emissive #000000` and NO emissiveMap, and the terrain is the same class WITH a `map` - so `emissiveMap` is the one channel the ground has and the buildings do not.** The terrain now carries a self-lit floor driven by its own satellite imagery (`emissive` grey, `emissiveMap = map`): it keeps its colour and detail and stops falling to zero, and because it is a floor rather than a fill light, shading and shadows still read on top. **0.30 chosen by eye against 0 / 0.16 / 0.30 / 0.55** at a straight-down vantage over the hill flank - 0.16 still too dark to read streets, 0.55 reads like daylight and fights the night. Live tuner `window.__earthGroundLiftApply(v)`; `window.__earthGroundLift = 0` restores the old look exactly. ⚠ `emissiveMap` is a program-cache-key term (`emissiveMapUv`), so this forks ONE extra terrain program, built behind the curtain. ⚠ The DUSK `tint`/`tintK: 0.90` pair is the HUB's sandwich terrain only (`_hzGrass/_hzRock/_hzSnow/_hzMoss`) - it never touched earth, so do not reach for it here.
- **(v47.15) ⚠⚠ KEEPING A WORLD ACROSS A ROUND MEANS RE-APPLYING EVERY PIECE OF *SHARED SCENE STATE* THE ROUND TEARDOWN RESETS.** The v47.13 `_keepTiles` win came with a regression I shipped and the owner found twice: *"in your preview window, i can see a weird wall, in earth/race"* and *"the water didn't load that time"*. **The mechanism is one sentence: `_swApplyAtmosphere` runs on EVERY round rebuild, its no-sandwich-terrain branch is what a real-world level always takes, and that branch RESETS shared scene state - while the only code that re-applied it lived inside `_lssGmapsBuildLevel`'s "the world was built fresh" branch.** So round 1 was always right and round 2 onward was wrong, which is exactly the shape that makes these look like two unrelated bugs. **Census that branch before adding anything to the keep path** - it resets fog, background, `_clearBrokenSimForcefield`, `_swDisposeHubWater` (*which also `_wxDispose()`s the weather*), `_setArenaGridVisible(true)`, `_skyDomeRefresh`, `_lssApplyHubLighting(false)`, `_lssRestoreArenaMood()`. Two of those were owned by the gmaps build and therefore broken; the sky was already self-healing in `_lssGmapsTick` (*"THE SKY CANNOT BE ALLOWED TO STAY GONE"*, v46.76), and lighting/mood/fog are not set by the gmaps build at all, so the set is complete at two.
  - **THE WALL was the ARENA BOUNDARY GRID** - six `LineSegments` (`userData.isArenaGrid`, 20,402 verts each) forming a **50,000-unit wireframe box at the world origin**, inside a level 297,000 units across, so its faces cut straight through Hong Kong. Fixed by **vetoing inside `_setArenaGridVisible`** rather than at the call sites: showing the grid is a *request*, and a streamed Earth has no arena edge to mark, whoever asks. That is ordering-proof, which chasing callers is not. ⚠ An **overlay** level (`_lssGmaps.overlayOnly`) keeps its grid - it still has a real arena underneath. ⚠ `_lssGmaps.cleanup` restores the grid, and it ran while `active` was still `true` (every caller clears the flag *after* calling it), so the closure now clears the flag on its FIRST line or the veto would hide the grid for good on the way out.
  - **THE SEA** is `_swBuildHubWater`, handed to LSS by `LSSEarthWorld.buildWater()` - which only runs when the TILES are constructed. Kept world = never constructed = no ocean from round 2. Fixed with a **self-heal in `_lssGmapsTick` beside the sky's**, not in the keep branch, so it does not depend on who disposes the water or in what order. ⚠ **Rate-limited**: `buildWater()` stands up a ripple sim, a reflector and two flocks, and returns `false` forever on a level with no sea - 2 s after a success, **30 s after a failure**, and `_lssGmaps._seaRetryAt` is zeroed on every build so a new level never inherits the last one's back-off.
  - **Probes:** `__gridState()`-style scene scans are in the transcript; the live tells are the console lines `[lss-gmaps] KEPT the world over <level>` (the broken path ran), `[lss-gmaps] sea vanished - rebuilt` and `[lss-gmaps] weather vanished - re-initialising`. `window.__earthKeep = false` forces the rebuild branch, which is the only in-session way to exercise `cleanup()` without leaving the map.
- **(v47.16) THE CAPTURE RING IS FRIEND-OR-FOE, NOT FLEET IDENTITY (`drawCircumpunctHUD`).** The champion-capture circle around the crosshair was coloured `_cc.isA ? red : green` - v39.56's *"the claiming fleet's colour (red A / green B)"* - so **a Fleet A player watched a RED ring fill while capturing their OWN objective, and a Fleet B player got green for the enemy taking theirs.** Both readings were inverted for exactly half the room, which is why it survived: whoever checked it was on Fleet B. Owner: *"if friendlies are capturing an objective, it should be a green circle on the HUD, but if an enemy is capturing it should be a red circle"*. **The fix was to read a field that already existed** - `_champCaptureState` has returned `mine` since v39.55 and **nothing had ever read it**. ⚠ Spectating is the one case with no friend or foe (`player.team` really can be unassigned - the arena lineup defaults it to A for that reason), so it keeps the old fleet colour rather than calling everything hostile. ⚠ The DOM bar (`#champ-capture`, `.cc-a`/`.cc-b`) is still fleet-keyed **on purpose**: it is hidden unless `window.__champBar = true` and its label says FLEET A / FLEET B, so there the colour is an identity readout, not a threat readout. **Verified by pixel count off `#circumpunct-hud`, all four combinations, 1617 arc px to 0:** mine-A/cap-A GREEN, mine-A/cap-B RED, mine-B/cap-B GREEN, mine-B/cap-A RED.
- **(v47.17-47.19) NRG + AMMO ARE TURNED PLATES, NOT CURVED CAPTIONS (`_hlfFlatPlate`).** Owner: *"put NRG text and AMMO text in the same orientation at the dash dots (rotated from what it's at), and remove the number readout for each"*. `_hlfLabelPlate` rides its text along the bar, which is right on the 136-degree top rows but means the 44-degree FLANK bars read almost **vertically** - the tangent at NRG/AMMO is ~115 degrees. The dash pip row in the same band is a straight strip at `_HLF_DASH.rot`, so both labels now take their tilt **from that constant** and cannot drift out of step with the thing they were told to match; they are MIRRORED (NRG `-`, AMMO `+`) the way the HUD already mirrors its flanks (`_HL.ab1.rot` -50 / `ab2` +50). ⚠ **The PLATE turns with the text** - rotating only the glyphs inside an arc cutout puts a ~1.4vm word across a 1.5vm cell at 85 degrees to the cell's own axis: it fits by arithmetic and reads as a mistake. Numbers dropped, which retired `plateDeg` (its only job was fitting a plate to a string whose length changed with the reading) and **leaves NO numeric ammo readout on the framed HUD** - deliberate, same call as the v35.42 note for hull.
  - **⚠ v47.18 REVERSED v47.01's "flush with the bar's OUTER EDGE" rule for these two.** That rule was right for an ARC cutout, where sharing the bar's edge is what made it look punched through; a plate turned off the bar's axis shares no edge with it, so the same offset just reads as misplaced. It showed up on AMMO and not NRG **because the two bands are different depths** - NRG is the band's inner half (11.2..13.2) so an outer-edge offset happened to land near the middle anyway, while AMMO spans the whole band (11.2..15.2) where it is 1.25vm off. Owner: *"NRG fits, AMMO is a off center in its bar"*. Each now takes its own bar's MID radius, which also puts AMMO at 13.2 - the dash row's own radius.
  - **The angular anchor is the end the bar READS ZERO from**, i.e. the end its fill grows from: NRG lights from `a0` (152), AMMO is `fromEnd` so it lights from `a1` (28). Owner: *"NRG can actually lower to the bottom of its bar" / "by bottom i mean where the bar would read 0"*.
  - **⚠ The HUD cannot be magnified with a CSS transform for inspection** - `_lssApplyShipRig` rewrites `hudCanvas.style.transform` every frame (the v35.03 parallax), so a scale set from the console is wiped on the next tick. `input.hudScale` caps at 1.75, and vmin sizing makes the HUD **scale-invariant to the viewport**, so `resize_window` buys nothing either. What works: `input.hudScale = 1.75` plus reading `#circumpunct-hud` pixels directly. **Measuring beats screenshotting here** - collect the near-white text pixels (`rgba(236,247,255,.95)`) in a window and take the principal axis for the tilt, the centroid for the position. Measured: NRG tilt **-31.1** at 152.4 deg / r 12.24, AMMO **+30.8** at 27.6 deg / r 13.11.
  - **Live knobs `window.__hudLbl = { slide, radial }`** (defaults 0.5 / 0.5 in `_HLF_LBL`): `slide` is how far past the zero end the plate hangs as a fraction of its own width (0 fully inside, 0.5 centred on the end, 1 clear of the bar), `radial` is the same across the band (0 inner edge, 1 outer). Added because this is eye-tuned against a 12-pixel word and a rebuild per nudge is the slow way to find a number nobody can derive.
  - ⚠ **The HUD lab (`hud_concepts.html`) does NOT view this.** Its extractor lifts `_HL` + `_hlDrawHUD` from `lss.js`; the shipped framed assembly is `_HLF` / `_hlfDraw`, which the lab's ORIGINAL and VARIANTS tabs do not carry. Tune `_HLF` in the GAME.
- **(v47.20) THE ROLE ICONS GREW OUTWARD, AND THE READY-POP STOPPED EATING THE NRG BAR (`_HLF_ICON_ROW`).** Owner: *"make the 3 icons slightly bigger, but don't make them overlap the NRG bar, they can expand outward"*. 1.85 -> **2.10vm**. The row is no longer CENTRED in the band's outer half: it is pinned by its **inner edge** (`rIn` = NRG's outer edge 13.2 + `GAP`) and every extra vmin travels outward, so size and the no-overlap rule stop fighting. At rest it reaches 15.50, past the 15.2 band edge - **free, because `_HLF.FR` only spans `TOP` 200..340 while this row sits at 152..196**, and the old `labR` 16.3 captions are long gone. ⚠ `GAP` is **0.20, not 0.10, because it has to cover the STROKE**: `_hlfIcon` strokes at `vm*0.17` centred on the outline, so the drawn edge reaches 0.085vm inside `rIn`. (The ready GLOW is a `shadowBlur` halo, not an edge - it washes over the bar by design and always did.)
  - **⚠ THE READY-POP WAS ALREADY OVERLAPPING, before any resize.** `pop` scales the icon up to **1.32x about its CENTRE** for 0.45 s, which put the inner edge **0.34vm inside the NRG bar** every time an ability came off cooldown - invisible as a bug because it is brief and looks like part of the flash. It now grows from the inner edge instead (`rDraw = IR.rIn + szV * pop / 2`), which makes the clearance **exact for any pop by cancellation**, not approximately right. `dPerStep` keys off `IR.rIn + szV/2` so the row's angular spacing tracks a live size change.
  - **Measured** by A/B-ing the rendered pixels through the live knob: lit samples in the 12.4..13.40 polar band next to NRG were **2651 at size 2.10 vs 2648 at size 0.40** - 0.1%, i.e. antialias noise plus the control's own stroke. The big icons add nothing beside the bar.
  - **Live knob `window.__hudIcon = { size }`**, same argument as `window.__hudLbl`: eye-tuned against a bar it must not touch.
- **(v47.21) THE FLAT-SCREEN HUD SHIPS AT 1.75x, THE TOP OF ITS SLIDER (`HUD_SCALE_DEFAULT`).** Owner: *"let's max out the HUD size by default in the settings (1.75x)"*. ⚠ **SIX places spelled this `1`** and only ever agreed by hand - the `input` default, `_hlScale`'s fallback, the settings page's build-time markup AND its reopen path, `saveSettings`, and `SHIPPED_DEFAULTS` - so they are one constant now, declared immediately above `const input` because `input`'s own initialiser reads it (v39.02 TDZ: a later top-level const read from an earlier initialiser throws, and `typeof` does not shield it). ⚠ **A SAVED SETTING STILL WINS.** `loadSettings` writes `data.hudScale` over the default whenever the key is present, which is every save written since v36.19 - so this changes FIRST BOOT, RESET TO DEFAULTS, and pre-v36.19 saves that have no key. **Anyone who has already moved the slider keeps their number: a default is not a migration.** Verified all three: no save -> 1.75 (and `SHIPPED_DEFAULTS` seeds 1.75 into storage); a save holding 1.0 -> **stays 1.0**; a save with the key deleted -> 1.75; settings slider reads `value 1.75 / max 1.75`, display "1.75x".
- **(v47.22) CORE IS A CHEVRON RUN (`_hlfChevronRow`).** Owner: *"i want the core bar to look unique... maybe like a sideways chevron pattern instead of a solid line"*. CORE was the third `{ solid: true }` `_hlfBarRow` in a row of them, so the gauge answering *"can I fire the big thing"* looked exactly like SHIELD. It is now a run of arrowheads pointing the way the meter FILLS (apex at the LARGER angle, because CORE grows `a0`->`a1`), which reads as a charge rather than a level and costs no extra colour. ⚠ **THE FILL IS CLIPPED, NOT QUANTISED** - lighting whole chevrons would turn a continuous meter into a ~15-step one, and CORE is exactly the gauge you watch climb. Every chevron is stroked as an empty track, then the whole run is re-filled inside a **pie-sector clip** at the true fraction, so the edge lands mid-chevron. ⚠ Geometry is given in **ARC LENGTH (vmin at the mid radius), not degrees**, so the pattern keeps its proportions if the row ever moves radius. Chevrons survive the 0.85vm row where the v47.01 hatch did not, because a chevron is a **shape**, not a texture. Live knob `window.__hudCore = { pitch, thick, depth }`.
  - **Verified STRUCTURALLY, not by eye**: count separate radial runs of lit pixels per angle across the lit span - a solid bar is `1` everywhere. Measured **0 runs x70 (gaps), 1 x141 (apexes), 2 x88 (the two arms), 3 x2 (antialiasing)** over 301 samples at `corePct` 0.62. That test distinguishes a chevron from a bar without a screenshot, which matters because **the HUD cannot be magnified for inspection** (see the v47.17-19 note).
- **(v47.23) CORE AT READY IS THE HULL'S BRIGHTEST SHADE, NOT YELLOW (`sh.coreHot`).** Owner: *"the yellow for core is wrong, it needs to correspond to the brightest of the theme's color scheme"*. **CORE was already themed while CHARGING** (`sh.core`) - the yellow only appeared the moment it filled, which is why it looked like a bug rather than a missing feature. The cause: `coreState` conflated FIRING and READY, and the READY branch in the data layer baked a literal `_hlA('#f0ff1f', pulse)`. **A data layer reaching past the theme layer to pick a colour.** Fixed by making READY emit a pulse **ALPHA** (`v.corePulse`) and letting the draw apply it to a themed shade, and by splitting `v.coreFiring` out of `coreState` (which stays, because `coreReady` still reads it for the glow).
  - **`coreHot` is DERIVED, not typed**: the `_HLF_THEME` table's own maximum lightness **plus a step** (0.72 -> 0.82), at CORE's hue offset and saturation. So it stays the brightest shade in the cluster even if the table is re-tuned. ⚠ It lives OUTSIDE `_HLF_THEME` deliberately - an entry in there would raise `lMax` and chase its own tail.
  - ⚠ **FIRING keeps its un-themed amber `#ffbe3c`**, on the same rule as the ability amber and the hull ramp in the "deliberately NOT themed" list: an ACTIVE state has to mean the same thing on every hull.
  - **Verified by sampling rendered pixels** on TRACKER (hull hue 32): CORE-ready **hue 32 / L 0.82**, HP **32 / 0.46** (`health [0,1.00,0.46]`), SHIELD **46 / 0.64** (`shield [20,0.92,0.64]`, and 32 + 20x0.69 = 45.8). The hue-offset x SPREAD arithmetic checks out to within a degree, and CORE outranks every other row in lightness. ⚠ **Sampling gotcha**: the ready pulse composites at `I.ga x 0.75..1.0` ≈ alpha 138-183, so an `alpha > 220` gate finds NOTHING in that row; and a "brightest pixel" heuristic picks the near-white LABEL TEXT unless you require `max-min > 30` and skip the plate at 270 deg.
- **(v47.24-47.26) THE CHARGE SHOT AND THE CLUSTER MISSILE LEAVE THE GUNS (`_powerShotMuzzle`).** Owner: *"blaster's charged shot looks like it comes from his center mass... it needs to come from the guns, marked G1, G2... in the glb"*, then *"cluster missile, same thing"*, then *"blaster's charged shot needs to shoot from all the gun spots at the same time"*. **The markers are `gun1..gunN`** (`/^gun\d+$/i` in `buildModelShipMesh` -> `userData.muzzleNodes`); G1/G2 is the owner's name for them. ⚠ **`blaster.glb` carries EIGHT**, puncture/pyro/tracker one each, slayer/syphon/vortex two - check before assuming two.
  - **`firePowerShot` spawned every tracer, pellet and net broadcast at `player.position`** while the CHARGE has sat on the markers since v37.68 (`_blasterChargeGlow` parents an orb to each). The weapon visibly charged at the barrels and fired out of the pilot's chest, which is what made it read as wrong rather than merely off. Long-range now fires **one beam per barrel, all converging on the same `end`** (the pale companion beam stays on barrel 0 only - one per barrel is 16 tracers for a single trigger pull); close-range cycles its 12 pellets around the rack.

The **90-degree turn** is the same snap on your own ship whenever that blend does NOT complete - in multiplayer the flight runs inside a fixed window and can be cut short, skipping the overwrite entirely.

A mesh pose alone does not stick: `Bot.update` runs `mesh.position.copy(this.position)` every frame, and `mesh.lookAt` only at speed > 1, so committing POSITION is enough and the slot orientation survives on its own until the ship moves.

Each slot is scored with `_spawnClearanceScore` first, and a slot that does not clear leaves THAT ship on its own validated spawn. One ship out of formation beats one ship inside a building.

Guarded now on the only thing that actually distinguishes a late joiner: **more humans on that fleet NOW than in the tally the deal used** (`game._botSeatHumans`, stashed by `spawnBots`). **Verified both clients: 4 bots, 2 a side, own fleet flanking at 109-233 u and the enemy at 2,400-2,600** - plus the log line `[dropin] no seat taken: fleet B has 1 human(s) and the deal already allowed for 1`.
  - ⚠⚠⚠ **FOUR WRONG DIAGNOSES BEFORE THIS ONE**, all of them plausible and all of them about the COUNT: a seat switched off, a hole in `deal.enemy`, `_lssHumanCounts` over-counting, `spawnBots` skipping index 0. The instrumentation that finally settled it took two steps: `[spawnBots] built:` at the END of the function proved the bot **was created** (turning "never spawns" into "removed"), and when the `Bot.destroy` tracer stayed **silent** it proved the removal bypassed the normal despawn path entirely.
  - ⭐ **THE TECHNIQUE WORTH KEEPING: trap the array, not the code.** No rebuild required - from the console, patch the live `game.entities.splice` to log a stack whenever it removes the id you care about, and re-patch when the array identity changes (`spawnBots` REPLACES it via `filter`). One run named the caller: `_dropinReplaceBot <- onComplete <- trystero data`. Auditing a dozen splice sites by hand had already failed twice.
- **(v47.40-47.41) THE LINEUP DOES NOT ANCHOR ON `sdfRoomData` - IT RE-ANCHORS ON THE PLAYER'S SPAWN.** Owner: *"i think they were in the game but somewhere else"*, then *"they were floating too high i think"* - and the altitude was the tell. **This is the fact that made three attempts miss:** once the player is in the lineup, the row is re-centred with `lineCenterX/lineY/lineCenterZ = player.position` (the "lineup on spawn | slide 0" block). So a peer centres its formation on **where it actually spawned**, while v47.39 centred that fleet's bots on the BOTS' CENTROID and v47.40 on the ROOM. Three origins for one formation. The authority now prefers that fleet's **own pilot** (its NetworkPlayer position) - the same point their client will use - with room and centroid as fallbacks for an all-bot side.
  - **(v47.40) FRAME THE FLEET, POSE ONLY WHAT YOU OWN.** v47.39 correctly stopped a peer posing proxies, which shrank `myShips` to one ship - and the cinematic's orbit radius follows that count, so the camera composed around a single hull and the fleet sat outside the shot. Owner: *"right tab bots were not in the cinematic"*. Framing now counts every hull on the fleet (owned, proxy, peer); posing still only touches owned ones.
  - **`window.__seats()`** (v47.40) reports `_lssHumanCounts()`, the resolved seats and the peer list with derived teams - `net` is closure-scoped, so a room's human tally could not otherwise be inspected, **least of all on a phone**.
  - **Measured at the cinematic's end on a real two-tab room**: the joiner's own bot **219 u away, dY +15**; the enemy fleet 2,241 / 2,269. ⚠ **But the log said it anchored `on their room`, not the pilot** - `net.networkPlayers` had no entry for that team at that instant, so the pilot path did not fire and the result came from room-approximately-equals-spawn, which only holds while the spawn pool is tight (v47.30/31). The pilot anchor is the belt-and-braces, not the thing that was measured.
  - ✅ **SOLVED in v47.43 - and it was NEVER a spawn problem.** See the `_dropinReplaceBot` entry below. Every guess that it was a seat-off, a hole in the deal, or a bad human tally was wrong; the bot was always built and then taken away.
  - ⚠⚠ **MEASURE AT THE BEAT, NOT AFTER IT.** Twice in this hunt I read positions in `playing` and reported them as cinematic-end values (once as "1,400 u away", once as a fleet "one bot short"). Post-launch the ships have been flying and the roster mirror has re-synced. Capture on the `CINE -> not CINE` edge.
- **(v47.30-47.31) GMAPS TEAM SPAWNS: TWO ENDS, AND THE FLEET ACTUALLY MOVES TO THEM.** Owner, two peers over Tokyo: *"they spawned right beside each other even tho opposite teams"*. Only the ASSAULT branch ever tagged `q.team` on the gmaps spawn pool, so elimination/classic reached `getValidSpawnPoint` untagged; worse, the non-assault placement was `const _s0 = _sp[0]` - **the same single point for everyone**, run locally on every peer. ⚠ Split by BEARING (origin -> furthest point), never by radius: the points are concentric RINGS, so a radius split puts two shells on one centre (the assault note measured 33 u apart). ⚠ **And CLUSTER each end** - the first cut took the top 35% by projection, which separated the ENDS correctly (8,479 u) while each end internally SPANNED 9,557 / 9,616 u, so your own wingmen were 3,664 and 8,109 u away. Take the N points nearest the extreme point instead. ⚠ **v47.31: re-place the BOTS too.** v46.89 re-picks the PLAYER once the pool is real ("the first pick happened before this world existed") - equally true of every bot, and only the player was covered, so the player teleported to their end and the fleet stayed at the pre-build origin. Splitting the ends without this makes the symptom WORSE, which is how it surfaced.

Two rules it established: `__prebake()`'s phase attribution is misleading on hub maps because every phase is priced in yielded GAME FRAMES, and a hub loading number read off the Browser pane understates the real one by ~3x.

Use it as a **reading copy** — this map is the high-level index; `index-working.html` is the line-level detail. The shipping `index.html` stays comment-stripped/lean.

## Architecture at a glance

- **One closure.** Everything from line 3036 to 70463 lives inside `_bootLSS()`. There are no ES modules, no `import`/`export` — every function, class, `const`/`let` shares one scope. `THREE` is the only true global (`window.THREE`, bridged in by a small `type="module"` script above `_bootLSS`).
- **Define-then-init.** The file *declares* ~950 functions + ~660 top-level `const`/`let` top-to-bottom, then **runs the real initialization at the very bottom** (`initAudio()`/`loadSettings()`/`buildShipSelect()` … `renderer.setAnimationLoop(gameLoop)` around **~L68910–69115**). Almost nothing executes until then.
- **~13 load-bearing singletons** hold all shared state (see the Singletons table). `game` (~2,900 refs) and `player` (~2,570 refs) are touched almost everywhere.
- **Frame flow:** `gameLoop` (**~L59523**) → updates every subsystem → `renderFrame` (**~L16800**) → `renderPostFX` / XR / direct path.
- **Perf profile:** the hub is **GPU-bound** on the dev machine. Diagnose live with `window.lssPerfSnapshot()`.

---

## ⚠ Critical rules & traps (read before editing)

1. **Init order is load-bearing.** The "define now, init at the bottom" model is why forward references work: `const audio` is declared at **~L60104** but used **~138×** earlier; `_spawnBossPortal` is defined at **~L34013** but *called* at ~L5763/5970/9145. **Don't reorder top-level blocks** without checking that nothing runs them before their declaration.
2. **Silent-no-op guards.** There are **~916 `typeof fn === 'function'`** guards around forward-referenced calls. A missing/renamed function **degrades to a silent no-op — no console error.** If you rename something, update *every* guarded call site, or a feature just quietly vanishes.
3. **Keep `antialias: true`** on the renderer (~L13340). The GPU birds/boids (**`_boidsVelFrag` ~L18943**) are MSAA-sensitive — disabling AA regressed combat *and* birds/forest.
4. **Never re-add object pooling for projectile/tracer VISUAL bundles** (`class Projectile` ~L25927, `spawnTracer` ~L35789). Pooling those regressed combat for bots *and* multiplayer. Per-shot allocation is intentional.
5. **Warmup must bind `postFX.rtScene`.** The "combat first-sight hitch" fix lives in `_shaderWarmup` (**~L26883**) and `_warmRealCombatFX` (**~L33546**); both must `renderer.setRenderTarget(postFX.rtScene)` so shader programs compile in the gameplay colorspace. Removing that bind brings the hitch back. **(v36.17) THE FULL RULE — three things fork a three.js program cache key without changing one character of GLSL, and all three must match the frame the effect will really be drawn in:** (a) the bound **render target** (null = sRGB output + tone mapping; any RT = linear + `NoToneMapping`), (b) **`scene.fog` presence** (a warm scene with no fog links a different program even for a fogged material), and (c) the **per-type LIGHT COUNTS** of the scene being rendered — `numDirLights`/`numPointLights`/`numSpotLights`/`numHemiLights` are in the key *even for unlit `MeshBasicMaterial`*, so an isolated warm scene is never a valid stand-in for the live one. Any warm render/compile of a gameplay material must therefore run against the **live `scene`** with **`postFX.rtScene` bound**. See PART 13's v36.17 entry for the probe that proves it.
6. **(v47.02) THE COROLLARY OF RULE 5: A WARM THAT BINDS THE WRONG TARGET IS PURE WASTE, AND IT COMPOUNDS.** `_warmRealCombatFXInner` used to compile AND draw the scene three ways — canvas at `NoToneMapping`, canvas at the live `ACESFilmic`, then `postFX.rtScene` — because a 2020-era comment assumed a direct-to-screen path existed. It does not: every live scene draw binds a target (`renderPostFX` -> `rtScene` on **both** branches, cineFX -> the composer RT, XR -> `xr.getRenderTarget()`), and `renderFrame`'s potato branch is unreachable because `applyQualityPreset` maps `'potato' -> 'low'` on its first line. **Measured: ~128 of the ~193 programs that phase created were dead; cyberpunk went 451 -> 331 programs at the curtain lift and its prebake 7,736 -> 2,409 ms.** The compounding is the lesson — `ms.carrier` 3,842 -> 195, `ms.cloak` 2,518 -> 112, `ms.drainCloak` 2,348 -> 1, because those phases were linking and draining the dead canvas variants of every hull. lss.map.md's own v39.81 water entry had already named this class of waste and left it open. ⚠ Two traps if you touch it again: the prebake's `drainFx0` drain must stay **unconditional** (it used to be gated on the finisher this change stops returning), and the `__fxWarmProgs` namer must sit BELOW the surviving compile or it names nothing. If a direct-to-screen scene path is ever revived, warm it there with ITS OWN target bound — toggling `renderer.toneMapping` alone never reproduced the combat key, which is why v36.17 added the `rtScene` bind.
7. **`_clip` name collision.** `_clip*` at **~L22110** = the *terrain clipmap* LOD system (`_clipGeo`/`_clipBuild`/`_clipUpdate`/`_clipmap`). `_clip` at **~L46572** = the *video recorder* (MediaRecorder). Totally unrelated — grep with care.
8. **(v47.02) `_stHash2i` JOINS THE SYNCED SET — and there are FOUR copies of the terrain math, not three.** `_stNoise2` now reads its 2x2 integer lattice corners through a direct-mapped cache `_stHash2i` (right under `_stHash2`) instead of calling `_stHash2` four times. It is **value-preserving by construction** — on a miss it computes the identical expression — and that was proven three ways: the height bake's own 48-point worker-vs-main-thread self-check, 5.96 M samples compared in node with **0 differing** and `Object.is`-equal float sums, and the unchanged 17,831,061-eval count. **Measured: the cold hub bake 16,064 -> 9,119 ms, `ms.clip` 12,980 -> 6,096, and the hub prebake stopped hitting `_PREBAKE_MAX_MS` — so the entity prime, the hull/cloak warm and the 14-pass GPU prime, all of which the hub had been silently SKIPPING, now actually run.** Its state hangs off the FUNCTION OBJECT, not a module `const`, so there is no temporal dead zone (rule: [`lss-tdz-const-trap`]) and `f.toString()` carries it into the worker strings. ⚠ The copies that must stay in step are the worker-string copy, the main-thread copy, `worldSDF`, **and `_hbFamily()`'s array** — adding a function there changes `_hbHash`, which invalidates the 34 MB IndexedDB height-bake cache exactly once. See [`performance_review.md`](performance_review.md).
9. **Triplicated terrain math.** `_st*` / `sdSphere` / `worldSDF` exist in **three copies** that must stay in sync: worker-string copy (~L17041), main-thread copy (~L17208), and the collision copy `worldSDF` (~L22496). Editing one without the others desyncs terrain vs. collision.
10. **Hub perf wins that stuck** (keep them): grass off by default, shadow map 2048², reflector throttle + RT shrink. Perf lives in `gameLoop`/`renderFrame`. **(v36.42)** the reflector throttle is now movement-aware (2..3 frames, not a flat 3) and the displaced water plane no longer renders into the reflection it samples — see PART 8's hub-water entries before touching any of it.
11. **A mode hook can end the match MID-TICK.** `updateRoundSystem`'s `'playing'` branch counts `aliveA`/`aliveB` at the TOP, then calls `activeMode().update(dt)` — and `EndlessMode` can call `returnToRootMenu()` from there, which resets `game.testMode`/`LSS.MODE`/`game.entities`/`game.state` underneath the rest of the branch. The `if (game.state !== 'playing') return;` guard right after the hook (v36.25) is what stops classic round-end firing into a torn-down world and leaving a ghost match running behind the menu. **Any new work added after that hook must sit BELOW the guard.**
12. **Fragile seams — re-verify after any combat/render edit:** (a) combat first-sight hitch, (b) hub framerate, (c) multiplayer combat. The sandbox renderer is useless for these; test in a real browser.
13. **(v36.29) NEVER hand-edit a `.glb` under `LSS/`.** Every shipped model is a BUILD ARTIFACT generated from `assets_src/` — see the Asset pipeline section below. Editing `LSS/**/*.glb` directly gets silently overwritten on the next run, and the pristine art only exists in `assets_src/`.

## Asset pipeline — GLB compression (v36.29)

`assets_src/` (repo root, **outside** the deploy tree) holds the **pristine originals** — 50 GLBs, 128.4 MB, byte-identical to the June art drop. Everything under `LSS/**/*.glb` is generated from it.

```
node tools/compress_glb.mjs          # rebuild all shipped GLBs   (one-time: cd tools && npm install)
node tools/compress_glb.mjs --dry    # report only, write nothing
node tools/compress_glb.mjs --only pyro
python tools/gen_manifest.py         # ALWAYS follow with this — refreshes preload sizes
```

Result: **128.4 MB → 40.7 MB on disk (−68%)**; preload manifest **90.6 MB → 63.5 MB**; total GLTF parse **810 ms → 647 ms**.

- **No runtime decoder.** Output is plain glTF plus `KHR_mesh_quantization` and `EXT_texture_webp` — both parsed natively by three.js r165, and both already shipping in this repo before the pass. Draco / `EXT_meshopt_compression` were rejected: they'd need a decoder wired into **all five** `new THREE.GLTFLoader()` sites, and a 404 decoder breaks every model.
- **Which slots survive is per-category and load-bearing** — three consumers disagree. `buildModelShipMesh` (~L29302) copies only `map`; but `bakeShipThumbnails` (~L29155) and **hub-city traffic** (~L26292) clone materials *as-is*, so hoard normal maps are live on 26 of 35 hub traffic ships. Dropping them saves 2.4 MB and silently replaces authored art with the procedural fallback — **don't**. `objects/Sphere.glb` is the one safe drop (`_champSelfIlluminate` collapses it to `MeshBasicMaterial({map})`).
- **Ship textures stay JPEG on purpose.** WebP decode costs ~25 ms vs ~10 ms for a 1024², worth it on the 1–3.5 MB hoard/monster PNGs but not on the ships' 0.42 MB JPEGs, where it saved 0.04 MB each and added **+16 ms parse each**. The `LOSSY_SOURCES` filter is PNG-only for that reason.
- **Two traps** (documented in the script header): `prune()` **must** get `{ keepLeaves: true }` or the empty `gun1`/`thruster1-4`/`cockpit1` marker nodes are deleted and muzzle/engine placement silently breaks; and the originals' non-spec `byteStride: 6` means a no-op round-trip on an already-quantized file *grows* it, so ships only win via `simplify`.
- **12 dead GLBs** (`objects/unanimated/**`, 6 unused rings) are in `assets_src/` only — unreferenced by code and absent from the manifest. `rings/fence.glb` still ships as a file but was removed from `OWNER_EXTRAS` in `gen_manifest.py`, so it is no longer preloaded (it has zero code references).
- **Bumping models:** drop new art into `assets_src/` at the same relative path, re-run both commands, then bump **`_MODELS_VERSION`** (not `LSS_BUILD`) so the cache-bust stamp moves.
- **(v38.92) The ship recipe JOINS cockpit parts per material** (`OVERRIDES.join`, `RECIPE_VERSION` 1.2). The c1seat hulls arrive as ~240 separate cockpit parts under a scaled/rotated `Cockpit_Root`: 244 draw calls and 244 mesh+material clones per spawn. `flatten` + `join` folds them to **14 primitives a hull** (what `buildModelShipMesh` clones and the GPU draws; the warmup log now says "14 ship meshes"). `join()` must run with `cleanup:false` or its own prune deletes the marker empties; the mesh-less leftovers are dropped by `dropJoinLeftovers` against `MARKER_RE`. WebP base-colour sources pass through untouched (no q88 generation loss). 66 MB of float32 exports -> 33.9 MB shipped. `assets_src/ships` was re-synced from the c1seat hulls on 2026-09-06 (source of truth).
- **(v38.93) TWO SHIP SETS, one stamp.** `OVERRIDES[ships/*].mobile = { baseColorMax: 1024 }` makes `compress_glb.mjs` write a second copy of each finished hull at `ships/m/<x>.glb` (base colour 2k -> 1k, ~-0.6 MB and a 4x cheaper decode each; 33.9 MB -> 29.7 MB for the set). `_shipsVariant()` (beside `_shipsBaseUrl`) returns `'m/'` when `_lssTexCap()` says small device (phone / standalone Quest / `window.__texCap.max` <= 1024 set before boot) and is memoised so `preloadShipModels()` and the manifest preloader agree; `gen_manifest.py` emits the small set as group **`ships_m`** and the preloader walks exactly one of `ships` / `ships_m` (64 entries either way). Both sets share `_MODELS_VERSION` - distinct URLs, so adding the 1k set needed no bump, but changing either set alone still does. Verified with the pane's mobile preset: `[ships] set: mobile`, only `ships/m/*` fetched, preload 44.2 -> 40.2 MB.
- **(v38.94) `cockpit1` is placed by the owner, baked into `assets_src/ships`** (a byte-exact glTF JSON edit of the marker's `translation`; the seats did not move). Model space: forward = -X, up = +Y. Blaster (x, +0.09), Puncture (-0.29, +0.09), Pyro (-0.08, +0.09), Slayer (-0.08, +0.09), Syphon (-0.33, +0.07), Tracker (-0.33, +0.03), Vortex (-0.46, +0.06). Re-running `compress_glb.mjs` carries them into both sets. The convention before this was "cockpit1 = hull bbox centre + a live `window.__cockpit.eye` nudge".
- **(v38.96) LEAN MOBILE SET.** `OVERRIDES.mobile = { baseColorMax: 1024, lean: true, cockpitRatio: 0.35 }`: standalone Quest / phones lost their GL context on the c1seat hulls. The `ships/m/` twin now keeps the base colour only (no normal map), has the clearcoat/specular/ior extensions stripped via `Extension.dispose()` so the loader builds `MeshStandardMaterial` (not Physical), a normal-tolerant re-weld and the non-hull primitives thinned to 0.35 (error 0.01) - ~80k tris a hull, **15.5 MB the set** (the pre-c1seat hulls were 18.7 MB). Note gltf-transform 4: `cloneDocument()`, not `doc.clone()`.
- **(v38.97) ROUND-TRANSITION HITCHES: ship pool + program retention.** Instrumenting the pane's GL context (linkProgram / bufferData counts per frame, `BufferGeometry.dispose` / `Material.dispose` stacks) showed every round transition disposing and rebuilding: bots (`spawnBots` -> `bot.destroy` -> `_disposeShipGroup` -> `new Bot` -> `buildModelShipMesh`, 14 meshes + 14 materials a hull now), obstacle clusters (`ClusterObstacle._buildChildren`, 232 geos), VR rocks (105 ShaderMaterials), terrain chunks (`resetSandwichTerrain` in `buildRoomGraphLevel`, 284 geos) and the launch warmup disposing its ghost-ship materials right after compiling them - each disposed material with no other holder FREES ITS PROGRAM, so the next round relinks it (16-19 links a transition, one of them a 224 ms cold link in `playing`). Fixes: `_botShipPool` (a dying bot parks its group by loadout|team|skin, the next bot takes it back; `_dimHullMat` reset), and `_lssRetainMat` applied to `_disposeShipGroup`, the obstacle rebuild, `_disposeVRRockMesh`, `Projectile.destroy` and the warmup ghosts. `_lssRetainMat` now retains by **three.js's own program keys** (`renderer.properties.get(mat).programs`, one material kept per real key in `window._fxRetainKeys`; the hand-rolled signature is only the fallback) - the signature could never mirror the real key (lights, fog, colourspace, UV channels, `customProgramCacheKey`), so the player's ghost-hull variants kept slipping through as duplicates and its round-start rebuild relinked 8 programs cold (a 1 s `player+weapons` frame). Result on the pane: **zero links at a round transition** (was 16-19), ship uploads gone; what remains is the 130 ms terrain/obstacle teardown. **Still per round and NOT ship-related:** the level itself is rebuilt every round (terrain chunks + obstacles + `_spawnBasinClouds` 765 sprites) - ~150 ms warm, a ~1 s pure-CPU frame seen in `warmup` - the next lever is skipping `buildRoomGraphLevel` when map/theme did not change.
- **(v38.98) Cockpit-part LOD + no interior shadows** (`buildModelShipMesh` tags every mesh whose material is `*_CP_*` as `userData._cockpitPart`, `castShadow=false`; `animateShipMesh` hides them past 300 u of the camera, shows inside 250). Measured at a frozen pose in a 5-bot arena: **-222k triangles and -18 draw calls a frame (-8.7%)** in the main pass, and the interiors' shadow-pass share is gone outright. The player's own ship is always in range of its camera.
- **(v38.98) Round-start facing.** `_facePlayerAtEnemy()` used to return without touching the heading when no live enemy was known (round 2+ on a non-authority client whose bot proxies arrive later, or any round where `respawnPlayer()` beat `spawnBots()` - the order varies), so the ship kept whatever heading the last round ended on. Now it falls back to the ENEMY TEAM'S SPAWN ROOM CENTRE (static `MAP_DATA` rooms), and the round>1 path re-faces right after `spawnBots()` while still in warmup.
- **(v38.99) KEEP THE TERRAIN BETWEEN ROUNDS** (`buildRoomGraphLevel`, `_keepTerrain`): when the round restarts on the same level object + biome + terrain mode with chunks resident and no pillar re-roll, `resetSandwichTerrain()`/`initSandwichTerrain()` and the T re-creation are skipped (only `_swApplyAtmosphere` + `_swSyncFX` run); rooms, race graph, bounds and `spawnDynamicObjects` still rebuild. Arena (Spire), gmaps, procedural, pillar maps keep the full rebuild. `window.__keepTerrain = false` restores the old path. Logs `[sandwich] terrain kept across the round (N chunks)`. **(v38.99) `_warmRealCombatFX` skips rounds > 1** once `_fxRetainKeys` holds >= 10 programs (the re-warm existed to recompile released programs, which no longer happens); `window.__fxWarmEveryRound = true` restores it. **(v38.99) Context-loss ladder** now steps every level down (`high -> medium -> low -> potato`) and a small device goes straight to LOW - the owner's phone was reloading on HIGH after every crash (`high | mobile ... classic/warmup` in both screenshots, i.e. the round transition).
- **(v39.00) LITE WARMUP ON SMALL DEVICES + async compiles** (`_warmupCombatShadersBody`): the owner's phone lost its GL context at `classic/warmup | up 25s` BEFORE the first match - the launch warmup adds 14 ghost ships (14 meshes each now), the model warm group and every FX pin at once and links every program in blocking `renderer.compile()` + render calls (37 s cold on the dev GPU), and Chrome kills a GPU process that stops answering. Small devices (`_fxSmallDevice`) skip the ghost fleet and the model warm group; the compiles the async body and the staged FX-pin slices can await go through `renderer.compileAsync` (parallel links, resolves when ready). `window.__fullWarmOnMobile = true` restores the full pass. Desktop warmup unchanged at ~3.5 s warm. Programs are retained (v38.97), so the first-sight compiles a phone now takes instead happen once per session.
- **(v39.01) PHONES WERE PINNED TO HIGH.** The boot-time quality restore (right after `applyQualityPreset`) promoted a stored `low`/`medium` to `high` on every launch - a pre-v36.09 legacy - which overwrote the phone's first-run LOW default, every LOW/MEDIUM picked in Settings and the LOW the context-loss ladder writes. Every crash overlay read `high | mobile`. Small devices now keep what is stored ; the desktop promotion is unchanged. (This is also why the v37.14 audit found "no reachable slow-PC preset" - LOW could never persist.)
- **(v39.02) PHONE CONTEXT LOSS - the regression window and the levers.** The owner's phone lost its GL context at round transitions (and once at launch) since v38; the v38.71 code already quotes the report. The window is **v38.60-38.64**: v38.60 turned the round rebuild from *detach* into *dispose + re-create* (rocks, organics, sprite textures, the outgoing hull) - on Android freed GPU memory is not reclaimed before the new allocations land, so the transition PEAK rose; v38.61 changed chunk streaming/readback; v38.64 the RT tiers (walked back for phones in v38.71). Quality was never the lever: LOW was promoted to HIGH at boot (v39.01) and on phones the tier does not resize the targets anyway. Measured resident set in one arena on the pane: ~98 MB geometry (72 MB terrain chunks), ~155 MB textures (PC 2k hulls), 174 programs. Fixes so far: terrain kept across rounds (v38.99), lean mobile hull set (v38.96), lite warmup + async compiles (v39.00), stored LOW respected (v39.01), **phones get the Quest budget tier and one terrain ring less** (v39.02). The crash overlay now prints `prog | heap | geoMB | chunks | tier | v` - read those off the next screenshot.
- **(v39.11) `bakeShipThumbnails` HAD BEEN RENDERING NOTHING.** `preloadShipModels` fits each prototype to its chassis `hullLength`, so `proto.scale` is ~85 for a canonical 2-unit hull. The bake measured the WORLD bbox (~170) and then called `model.scale.setScalar(180/170)` - **replacing** that 85x scale instead of multiplying it - leaving the ship ~2 units long in front of a camera at 320. Every thumbnail was a transparent PNG (0 opaque pixels of 3072 sampled, ~7 KB) and nothing errored. `multiplyScalar` fixes it (54.9 KB, 209 opaque). It also set `scene.environment = sceneEnvMap`, a PMREM **render-target** texture owned by the MAIN renderer that a second context cannot upload - and these hulls are metallic PBR, which renders near-black with no environment; the bake now builds a small sky gradient through its OWN `PMREMGenerator` (avg brightness 20 -> 60). This fed the teammates strip as well as the v39.09 mobile ship-select fallback.
- **(v39.12) Third-person first-switch hitch on phones.** Skipping `_ghostPinWarm` on small devices (v39.05) moved its cost to the first time the chase camera pushes into the hull: 6 programs linked, 40 ms + 56 ms frames. `_ghostPinWarmAsync` does the same ghost-hull warm through `renderer.compileAsync` - parallel links, never blocks the GPU, so no watchdog risk. Note it reproduces only intermittently: the game already starts in third person, so those programs sometimes compile during the launch cinematic instead.
- **(2026-09-06) PERF REVIEW findings still open:** (a) the level is rebuilt every round (`buildRoomGraphLevel` -> `resetSandwichTerrain` 284 chunk geometries, `spawnDynamicObjects` 232+105 obstacle/rock geometries, `_spawnBasinClouds` 765 sprites) - ~130 ms warm, up to ~1 s in a frame - skip it when map+theme are unchanged; (b) cold start links 156-176 programs synchronously in the launch warmup (3.4 s warm, 37 s cold on the pane) - `renderer.compileAsync` / KHR_parallel_shader_compile would overlap it with the countdown; (c) arena frame is ~2 M triangles at ~400 draw calls with 5 bots, ships ~440k of it after the LOD, terrain+obstacles the rest; hub CPU is ~3.5 ms a frame (renderFrame 1.9, ripple 0.3-0.75) and vsync-capped at 144 on the dev GPU at pane size - the hub is GPU-bound only at full resolution.
- **(v38.94) Glass by look, not by name** (`buildModelShipMesh`): any transparent ship material under 0.5 opacity gets `depthWrite: false`, not just `canopy_glass`. The c1seat panes (`*_Windshield_LaminatedGlass` 0.08, `*_CP_HUDGlass` 0.10) were writing depth a hand's width from the eye, so every transparent effect sorted after them - fire clouds and the tether trap (`renderOrder` 1), beams (2) - failed the depth test and vanished from first person.

`gen.cos` (seed^0x41C64E6D) feeds themes/god-rays/storm bolts in `EndlessMode._world`. **Wave authority:** `amStasisOwner` (lowest peerId) alone runs `_director`/`_spawnWave`; `_spawnWave` + the cleared transition call `_botSendRoster()` (the sweep kills peers' dead proxies); the four campaign bot-sync gates (`_botNetSync`, `_botSendRoster`, `bot_roster`, `bot_state` handlers) are now `(net.campaign || net.endless)`; non-authority peers run `EndlessMode._coopPhase` — phase/banners/hull-patch DERIVED from proxy-bot liveness, no spawn, no clock. **Teams:** `assignTeamFromPeerOrder` + `_teamForPeerId` early-return `TEAM_FLEET_A` for `net.campaign || net.endless` — this also FIXES campaign co-op, whose joiners were silently seated on FLEET B (hostile to host, friendly to the hoard) by the open-solo challenger rule. **Lives/distance are PER-PLAYER v1**: out-of-lives in a room = RUN OVER banner + spectate via the death cam (the 6s `returnToRootMenu` soft-return is solo-only now); teammates fly on. `#btn-ss-bots` hidden in endless (mirrors the spawn gate; its `elim_bots_off` nulled `openSoloHostId` under the drop-in machinery). `net.endless` declared on the singleton, cleared in `_cancelRoomForLocalPlay` + `EndlessMode.onTeardown`. **Campaign entry finding:** the co-op door already existed — `startCampaignJourney` routes roomed/code-typed players to `startCampaign()` → `_startHostedMode()` (v32.76 authority PvE) before any journey cinematic arms; only the FLEET-B team seat (above) was broken. Known v1 quirks (documented in `endless_mode_design.md`): waves anchor to the authority's ship; a dead/out authority pauses new waves; mid-run drop-ins start at the cavern mouth; `bot_fire` replay suppression keys on `openSoloHostId`, which can differ from `amStasisOwner`.

- **(v36.06) LONG-RUN ROUTE RECOVERY** (owner bug: "choppy 45-53km in, then no enemies, and it stopped counting my km") — the bounded wander's seam, diagnosed + closed. **Jump:** `_reanchor(run)` (EndlessMode method, above `_director`) · the RELOCK else-branch in `update`'s progress block · the WAVE LOST branch in `_director` · the self-avoidance block in `_lssEndlessNextSeg`. **Diagnosis** (offline byte-exact sim of gen+tracker, then live headless harness): past 42k from origin the heading biases home; the free-path pivot (v35.73) means a pilot flying their own valley line diverges exactly where the invisible spine turns — the 3-seg × 4200u tracker window loses the lock FOREVER (no recovery path existed): dist freezes (live repro: frozen at 39.15km while 80km flown), the window parks (gidSpan pinned), waves anchor to the stale knot 10-40km behind (spawn measured 11,290u away → director stuck in `battle` for 30+ km = "no enemies after that"), and extension stalls so the append-rebake churn stops (= "not choppy anymore"; the 45-53km chop IS that churn while the folded route end lingers near the strayer). **Fixes, all v36.06:** (1) RELOCK — after 4s unlocked while moving, re-scan the whole tracked window FORWARD of the lock (first match); credit the straight CHORD flown since loss, capped by the skipped spine arc (monotone, no unflown credit). (2) RE-ANCHOR — pilot >5200u from EVERY tracked seg for 5s (solo only — a re-anchor derives from local position and would fork the v35.85 shared route; co-op keeps old behavior, documented seam): credit the lost chord (speed-capped 600·lostT), free every tracked seg (bolts + carve shapes + `_swInvalidateChunksInRect` over each removed shape's influence rect — removal is a heightfield change too, the v35.84 rule), restart the generator ~2600u AHEAD of the ship on the flight heading, 8 fresh segs via `_lssEndlessApplySeg`, progGid −1 (re-locks next tick, zero windfall), lastHall = player pos, banner THE CAVERN SHIFTS + `endless_reroute` announcer; gen.nextGid keeps counting (monotone-gid invariant), gen.vis history kept. (3) WAVE LOST — battle wave whose every live bot is >14km away for 10s: destroy+splice stragglers (roster-sweep pattern; vanish-without-dead-tick = aegis drops them uncounted), back to `travel`, no clear reward. (4) SELF-AVOIDANCE — `_lssEndlessNextSeg` steers the candidate endpoint away from visited 4.2k-cells (fixed deflections ±0.5/±1.0 toward the turning side, ZERO extra rand() draws, visited set derives from route state in gid order = co-op byte-identical; FIFO 256; last-3 cells exempt). (5) `a._pres` stale-stamp sweep every 512 frames (was one key per bot id ever). **Proof** (headless harness: loop stopped via `setAnimationLoop(null)`, spine-follow + deliberate 63° strays at bias onset, `__endlessTick` batches + `__swStream` manual drain, 2km logging): pre-fix (recovery timers pinned −1e9) = the exact owner symptom chain above; post-fix 95.2km arc → 93.35km credited (98.1%), dist monotone, 2 strays → 2 seamless re-anchors (freeze spans bounded 5.7/8.1km, chord credited on recovery), all 7 wave spawns ≤5,219u from the player, segs ≤15 / cyls ≤15 / chunks ~650-706 steady / bolt pool 5 / pres swept 42→12, wave-lost clean (`battle→travel` at exactly 10.0s, 6/6 despawned), then live-loop resume → WAVE 11 fought at the player, RUN OVER path wrote best 99.51km, zero console errors. `__endlessInfo()` grew dist/progGid/segs-span/lostT/farT/reanchors/phase/waveN/cyls/ents/chunks/rebaked/pres for harnesses. ⚠ the offline sim pair lives in the session scratchpad (`endless_sim.js` / `endless_sim_fixed.js`) — port them forward if the generator's draw ORDER ever changes (they must stay byte-exact to be evidence).

See the v36.13 entry below). Debug: `window.__endlessStasis()` (live fields + containing hall gid + SDF, every windowed hall with its gate roll and ahead/behind state, the spawn timer, and `spot` = where the NEXT spawn would land).
- **(v36.38) AEGIS CAP RAISED 5 → 10 + THE AT-MAX REWARD LADDER** (owner: "in endless mode I got stuck at aegis level 5, taking more powerups didn't level me up"). v35.90 hard-walled the surge at L5 and every further bolt did **nothing, silently** — no rank, no alternative, no feedback — which in a mode about endless progression, with bolts as deliberately rare off-route treasure, reads as a bug. **Jump:** `const _EAEGIS_MAX` (the curve block, immediately above `const EndlessMode`) · the collect body in `_aegis` · `_aegisSetLvl` · `_endlessAegisDmgOut` · debug `window.__endlessGrab(n)`. **The curve is now table-driven and TAPERED** — `_EAEGIS_DMG` / `_EAEGIS_SPD` / `_EAEGIS_REG`, indexed by rank, replacing the three flat `k * lvl` expressions. **L1-L5 are byte-identical to v35.90** (+6% dmg / +4% speed / 0.30 %/s regen each) so the shipped early game does not move; L6-L10 shrink hard (dmg +5/+4/+3/+2/+1 pp, speed +3/+2.5/+2/+1.5/+1 pp, regen +0.20/+0.15/+0.10/+0.10/+0.05), landing L10 at **dmg ×1.45 · speed ×1.30 (455 from 350) · regen 2.10 %/s**. Balance rails: `_spawnWave` caps wave size at `min(6, 2+floor(dist/3000))` (i.e. hostile pressure is bounded by 12 km while the route is not), the whole L6-L10 stretch buys only +11.5% DPS / +8.3% speed over L5 for FIVE more finds, and speed ×1.30 stays UNDER the hoard bot's shipped 1.33 (`_campTuneHoardBot`) — the same rail v35.90 used for L5's 1.20. Route bolts gate at ~28% of 2000-4000 u segments (~1 per 10 km), so L10 is a ~100 km run spent leaving the lane and chasing fleeing motes. **A bolt at true max is never worthless again — three-step ladder in the collect body:** `lvl < MAX` → rank up (unchanged) · `lvl = MAX && lives < run.livesMax` → **+1 LIFE** · `lvl = MAX && lives = livesMax` → **+250 m scored `run.dist`** (accumulate-only, so a `+=` is safe). **The life cap protects the difficulty contract:** `run.livesMax = _endlessLivesCapFor(startLives) = 2 × startLives` (EASY 6 / MEDIUM 4 / HARD 2), so the EASY>MEDIUM>HARD ordering AND ratio survive exactly and a HARD run can never become a MEDIUM one; the cap is on the LIVE count (not on grants), so after a death a max-rank pilot can keep converting exploration into survivability, bounded above. **Feedback everywhere** (silence was the actual bug): the HUD tag gains ` MAX` at the ceiling and appends the reward (` ⚡ +1 LIFE` / ` ⚡ +250 m`) for `a.rwT` seconds, plus an `AEGIS OVERFLOW` banner and a distinct sound per branch (`round_start` for the life, `upgrade_core` for the distance, `rearm_reset` on every bolt as before). Co-op safe (placement is still the pure gid hash; ranks + lives are per-player) and the reversible-buff discipline is untouched. Verified live (150 km EASY run): the whole 15-bolt ladder walked through production code — L1..L10 at speed 364/378/392/406/420/430.5/439.25/446.25/451.5/455 and dmg 1.06→1.45 and regen 0.3→2.1 %/s, then +1 LIFE ×3 (3→4→5→6 = cap), then +250 m ×2 (dist 107592→107842→108092); HUD read `150.91 km · LIVES 6 · AEGIS L10 MAX ⚡ +1 LIFE` in the flash colour with the OVERFLOW banner up; death → L10 + the same clone reference + speed 455 survive and a life is spent; teardown → the EXACT base chassis reference restored (350) with `curCh` null; zero console errors.

#### Match-start flows & ship-select entry — `~L6829`
**Jump:** `function startSolo` · `function enterShipSelect` (~L6988) · `function startAssault`
- **Symbols:** `startSolo`, `startTest`, `startRace`, `startAssault`, `_startHostedMode`, `enterShipSelect`
- **(v35.20) ELIMINATION** — **Jump:** `async function startElimination` (just after `startOpenSolo`). MULTIPLAYER PvP + MULTIPLAYER AND BOTS merged into one menu entry. Follows `startOpenSolo`'s room handling (create-or-reuse, then straight to ship-select) but **honours a code typed in `#room-code`** instead of overwriting it — `startOpenSolo` always minted a fresh code, silently discarding what the user typed. No code required: blank mints one. Falls back to `startSolo()` if the room can't open. Symbols: `_elimGenCode`, `_elimWantBots`, `_setEliminationBots`, `startElimination`, `_renderEliminationBotsBtn`, `_toggleEliminationBots`.
- **⚠ (v35.20)** The button **keeps the id `#btn-join`** deliberately — `#btn-join.lss-ready-cta` styling hangs off it and `joinRoom()` still toggles its `disabled`. `#btn-opensolo` and `#mp-join-msg` are deleted; `startOpenSolo` itself is KEPT (the `open_solo_start` netcode path and `_startHostedMode` still reference it).
- **(v35.20) No lobby READY button.** `joinRoom()` used to relabel `#btn-join` to "CLICK WHEN READY" 500 ms after connecting and wire it to `toggleReady()`; that's removed so ELIMINATION keeps its label. **`updateReadyButton()` is now a deliberate no-op stub** — it was the only thing rewriting that text, and `toggleReady()` (its only caller) is now unreachable from the UI. The ready HANDSHAKE is untouched: readiness is signalled by committing a loadout on ship-select (the loadout broadcast IS the ready signal). Instead, `_renderRoomBox` swaps **CREATE / JOIN → "SELECT GAME MODE BELOW"** (`.lss-room-joined`: green, `pointer-events:none`) once `net.active && net.roomCode`. That swap is set *outside* the signature early-return so it survives a bailed re-render, and `_renderRoomBox` runs on a 1500 ms interval. The in-room peer line also changed from "use CLICK WHEN READY below" to "pick a mode to head to the hangar".
- **(v35.20) Bots toggle** — `#btn-ss-bots`, docked in **`#ss-header-right` under CONFIRM & LAUNCH** (top-right of ship-select), rendered by `_renderEliminationBotsBtn` from `enterShipSelect`. Label stays **"ADD BOTS"** in both states with a ticked/unticked box prefix (`☑`/`☐`) — swapping the wording made it ambiguous whether it described the state or the action. `.ss-bots-on` tints it green. Shown for every mode EXCEPT `campaign`/`freeflight` — classic, race and assault. **Deliberately NOT gated on `net.active`:** `startRace`/`startAssault` run SOLO (`net.active=false`) whenever no room code is entered, which is exactly where you want to switch bots off.
