### What is NOT ours, established three independent ways

Chrome's GPU process on this machine stalls for seconds: `GPU Process/CrGpuMain` `RunTask` events of
**2.2-3.9 s** in the owner's own DevTools trace; a second, idle 1x1 WebGL context whose fence stalls
to the same millisecond as the game's (including one submitted MID-stall); and overlay boxes
rendering their background with no text. DuckDuckGo, same engine, same page: smooth. Nothing in the
page can fix that - the levers are `chrome://flags/#use-angle` → Vulkan, clearing ShaderCache/GPUCache,
Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling, and pinning Chrome to the discrete GPU.

⚠ **The revert to 40.44 was correctly declined**: the ball bug's functions have zero diff hunks since
40.44, the countdown bug arrived with v40.57 (after it), and the desktop symptom is the browser. A
revert would have cost every verified fix and repaired none of the three live bugs.


## v40.90 / v40.91 — the fullscreen settle ladder, and per-frame pass shapes in a mark

### v40.91 — FULLSCREEN NEVER RAN THE SETTLE LADDER

Owner, on a phone: *"the countdown and touchscreen controls only appear if you're NOT in fullscreen,
or if you switch away from full to not full to full again then you can have them in full screen"*.
That recipe IS the diagnosis: the layout is computed once against the wrong viewport, and only a
SECOND transition corrects it.

This file already knows the failure mode. `_viewportSettle`'s own note: *"mobile browsers often fire
orientationchange while innerWidth/Height still hold the OLD orientation's values, and don't always
fire a final resize once they settle"* - and the remedy is a LADDER of retries (0 / 250 / 700 ms).
But that ladder was wired to **`orientationchange` only**:

| event | what ran |
| --- | --- |
| `orientationchange` | `_viewportSettle` (laddered 0/250/700) |
| `resize` | `_applyViewportSize` — **one shot, no ladder** |
| `visualViewport resize` | `_layoutSticksSoon` (laddered) |
| **`fullscreenchange`** | **nothing** — only the incidental `resize` |

So entering fullscreen got a single un-laddered `_applyViewportSize`, and `_layoutSticks` - which
pins every stick and button in px - **never re-ran at all**. Toggling fullscreen off and on just buys
more events, which is exactly the owner's workaround.

⚠ **Corroborated by the file itself**, three lines from the fix, in a v35.06 note: *"window-level
resize/orientationchange events get eaten by FULLSCREEN TRANSITIONS"*. That was written about the
sticks missing rotations; it is the same mechanism making the fullscreen transition under-notified.

v40.91 hooks `fullscreenchange` / `webkitfullscreenchange` to BOTH ladders - `_viewportSettle` for the
canvas and camera, `_layoutSticksSoon` for the touch controls. Both are idempotent (they only write
left/top/width/height), and `_applyViewportSize` has been dirty-checked since v40.75, so the extra
calls are free when nothing moved. **Verified:** a dispatched `fullscreenchange` gives
`__vpSize [1, 4]` - one real reallocation, four correctly skipped.

### v40.90 — per-frame render-pass shape, in every mark

Three live pass-recorders in a row were wiped by page reloads, so it is in the recorder now: wrap
`renderer.render`, and on each rAF close out the frame's list of targets into one string. Emitted as
`pass: [t, shape, totalDrawCalls]` for the last ~4 s.

Read it for the countdown flicker. Measured live in elimination before this shipped:

```
~1.5 s before "2":   4608x2424>C                     (shadow map STRAIGHT TO CANVAS, no postFX)
during "2":          4608x2424>S>S>S>C>K             (the full chain)
```

The pipeline changes shape inside the countdown - tone mapping, bloom and colour change with it. And
an extra leading `S` pass appears on alternating frames (the water Reflector, +550 draw calls: 893 vs
342, 201 swings of 1.3-1.6x across 416 frames). `S` = rtScene, `C` = canvas, `K` = the keep-warm 512.


## v40.92 — THE WATER FLICKER AT "2". Found in a mark, mechanism traced, guard verified.

Owner: *"something in the water flickers, at 2"*. v40.90's per-frame pass recorder caught it on the
first try, and **three independent marks agree**:

```
n139  51.59  calls=787  960x540>S>128x128>960x540>S>960x540>960x540>960x540>C>K
n142  19.50  calls=846  960x540>S>128x128>960x540>S>960x540>960x540>960x540>C>K
n145  28.30  calls=903  960x540>S>128x128>960x540>S>960x540>960x540>960x540>C>K
```

Identical signature, exactly one occurrence per run, always in `warmup`. Every normal frame renders
the scene ONCE (`S`); that frame renders it **twice**, at 787-903 draw calls against a normal 307-620.

The extra `S` is `_warmDrawRoot` - and the `960x540` immediately in front of it is **the water
Reflector refreshing inside that render**, off `_warmDrawRoot._cam`: a throwaway PerspectiveCamera
parked at `(c.x, c.y + r*0.5, c.z + r*2.6)` looking at the ship, hundreds of units from the real eye.

The mirror renders its RT from there **and caches that position as `_reflEyeP`**. On the next real
frame the cadence gate measures the true camera against the WARM camera, finds it inside the 90 u
jump threshold, and skips its refresh - so the water samples a reflection captured from a viewpoint
the player is not at. `uReflFloor` puts that layer in every water pixel, so it reads as the whole
surface flashing for a frame or two.

⚠ **This is why v40.49's jump test never fixed it.** That test was written for the LAUNCH camera cuts
and it works for those. Nothing anticipated a warm pass hijacking the mirror *between* two real
frames - the cut it needed to notice happened inside a render it never saw.

**Fix**: `_warmDrawRoot` raises `window.__lssWarmDraw` around its `renderer.render`, and the
reflector's cadence gate returns early while it is set. The warm needs the hull's programs, not a
reflection. Returning leaves `_reflGap` untouched, so the next real frame is due on the normal
cadence and the cached eye still describes the last REAL eye.

**Verified live** by driving the guard directly:

| | frame shape |
| --- | --- |
| flag off | `26x26>26x26>`**`532x344`**`>S>532x344...` — mirror present |
| **flag on** | `26x26>26x26>`**`S`**`>532x344...` — **mirror absent** |
| flag off again | `26x26>26x26>`**`532x344`**`>S>532x344...` — mirror back |

⚠ Note the pass ring holds 400 frames (~3 s), so "0 double-scene frames" in a late sample proves
nothing - the warm frame scrolls out. Check `__cloakWarm` for whether the warm ran at all, and drive
the guard directly rather than waiting for the frame.


## v40.93 — the audit caught a bug I shipped, and corrected my mechanism

An adversarial audit of the v40.92 water fix confirmed the diagnosis and returned three corrections.
Two were right and one was wrong; all three were checked rather than taken on trust.

**✓ REAL BUG, MINE, HIGH SEVERITY.** v40.84's `_restoreMats` branch read:

```js
if (ud && ud._cloakOrigOpacity !== undefined && m.opacity < m._wOp) { ...hand over baseline... }
else { m.transparent = false; m.opacity = m._wOp; }
```

`m.opacity < m._wOp` was meant to mean "a cloak is live, let it keep control". It does not. At restore
time the warm has JUST set `m.opacity = m._wOp * 0.01`, so **it is always true** - and every material
that had ever cloaked was skipped and left at one percent, transparent, permanently. The first cloak
of a match armed it; every warm after that stranded the ship.

⚠ It never appeared in testing because `_cloakOrigOpacity` only exists once `_setShipMeshOpacity` has
actually run - i.e. after a real cloak - and the v40.88 verification (864 frames, minimum opacity
never below 0.08) was free flight with no combat. **The branch was never entered.**

Fixed by always restoring; the baseline hand-over stays (that part of v40.84 is still correct). Safe
because of v40.88: flip and restore are one synchronous call no frame can observe, and
`_setShipMeshOpacity` re-applies every frame while cloaked. Proven in isolation against both versions:

| material | old | v40.93 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| has cloaked before | **opacity 0.01, transparent** | opacity 1, opaque |
| never cloaked | opacity 1, opaque | opacity 1, opaque |

**✓ MECHANISM CORRECTION.** My v40.92 comment said the next real frame skips its refresh because the
jump test measures against the warm eye. Backwards: the warm eye is hundreds of units away, so the
90 u test FIRES and the mirror does refresh. The artefact survives on DRAW ORDER - the displaced sheet
copies `_reflWorld`/`tDiffuse` BEFORE the Reflector's own onBeforeRender, so the frame after a warm
draw samples the warm-eye capture through the warm-eye matrix. The file already said so beside the
sheet ("THIS SHEET draws first", and the jump escape "shortens the artefact to ONE frame ... it does
not reach zero"). The fix is right under either reading; the comment is now corrected.

**✗ REFUTED.** The audit claimed `grep -c __lssWarmDraw index.html` = 0, so "the owner is playing an
unguarded build". It grepped the wrong file: this project splits the JS out via `strip.py`, and
`lss.js` contains the guard 3 times. ⚠ Any agent auditing this repo must be told about the two-file
split, or it will report shipped code as missing.

Also refuted by the audit, correctly: `rt4608x2424` is `postFX.rtScene` at MEGA, **not** a shadow
atlas (there is one shadow map, 2048x2048, rendered inside `renderer.render`); and the 2-pass
`...>C` frames are ones where `renderFrame` never ran because `_lssPickerOwnsFrame()` held it, not a
postFX toggle. My earlier "the pipeline changes shape mid-countdown" reading was wrong on both counts.


## v40.94 — hide without destroying the layer (the fullscreen touch/countdown glitch)

Owner: *"it only shows the countdown and touchscreen controls if you're not in full screen...
starting full screen after not being in full screen will keep the touchscreen controls and countdown
active"*. Both halves are one fact: **`display: none` DESTROYS the element's compositor layer**, and on
this device a layer first created while the page is ALREADY fullscreen never gets rasterised - while
one that already existed survives the transition intact.

The visibility tick did `root.style.display = show ? 'block' : 'none'`, and the v35.15 note beside it
already said exactly when: *"the intro cinematic hides the overlay exactly while round start releases
the orientation lock and Chrome settles fullscreen"*. So the controls are undisplayed during the
cinematic and re-displayed mid-fullscreen - precisely the case that cannot come back. `#ship-select-
countdown` is the same shape: `display: none` for the whole match, `display: block` at the launch beat.

⚠ Same mistake as the v40.65 repaint kick (withdrawn in v40.72), which destroyed layers on purpose.
**On this hardware, never make the compositor rebuild a layer you still need.**

Both now hide with `visibility: hidden; opacity: 0` and stay `display: block`. `visibility` INHERITS,
so the `.tc` children (which carry `pointer-events: auto`) stop hit-testing exactly as they did under
`display: none` - the behaviour the JS relied on is unchanged. The three JS sites that read/wrote
`root.style.display` now read/write a `.tc-on` class instead.

**Verified** (desktop, forced with `?touch=1` since the touch module only builds on touch-capable
devices):

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| base rule parsed, font-family intact after the brace | ✓ |
| `#touch-controls.tc-on` is a separate rule | `visibility: visible; opacity: 1` |
| child `.tc` rule still parses (nothing swallowed) | ✓ |
| root off → on | `block/vis:hidden/op:0` → `block/vis:visible/op:1` |
| **child hit-testing** | `hidden` when off, `visible` when on |
| button while hidden in warmup | `153x104@532,16` — laid out, layer alive |
| countdown off → `.active` | `block/vis:hidden/op:0` → `block/vis:visible/op:1` |

⚠ **`node --check` cannot see CSS.** The first attempt put the `.tc-on` rule INSIDE the unclosed
`#touch-controls` block (the base rule spans several array entries and the `}` is on the font-family
line). It passed every gate and would have shipped broken. When editing the injected stylesheet
strings, always read back the PARSED rule from `document.styleSheets`.


## v40.96 — the measurement WAS the workaround

Owner: *"when it's on this debug mode, the touch screen controls and other missing items flash on and
off"*. That one sentence is the diagnosis, and it also explains why five builds of readouts all came
back "correct".

The v40.95 geometry probe, on the phone in fullscreen:

```
VV   1089x485 off:0,0 pg:0,0 scale:1   win:1089x485   scr:1090x486
BOX  H:1089x485@0,0/fixed/ov:hidd      B:1089x485@0,0/fixed/ov:hidd
```

Visual viewport, layout viewport, screen and both containing boxes all agree; the controls are laid
out exactly where they belong - and without the readout they are not painted. **The elements are
correct and the browser is simply never scheduling their paint.** The WebGL canvas updates through
GL, which dirties no DOM, and a static overlay whose content never changes gives the compositor
nothing to re-rasterise.

The debug readout is the only difference, and what it does is call `getBoundingClientRect()` and
`getComputedStyle()` on these very elements every 100 ms - both force a style/layout flush.

⚠ **A FORCED READ, NOT A DISPLAY TOGGLE.** v40.65 tried to force paints with `display:none` + restore
and had to be withdrawn in v40.72, because that DESTROYS the layer - the one thing this hardware
cannot rebuild. `void el.offsetHeight` flushes layout without touching the box, the layer or any
animation. It is exactly what the readout does by accident.

Three sites, all cheap: the touch overlay's existing 250 ms visibility tick (one forced layout 4x/s,
and only while the controls are up), every `_cdPaint` beat, and each `_layoutSticksSoon` ladder step
(which is what covers the fullscreen transition).

**Verified on 40.96:** countdown `active|3 -> 2 -> 1 -> LAUNCH`, `tc-on` engages and holds,
`visibility: visible / opacity 1`, `touchActive: true`.

⚠ Honest status: this is a WORKAROUND for a browser paint-scheduling failure, not a root fix, and it
is the third attempt at this symptom (v40.91 settle ladder, v40.94 layer preservation, now this).
The difference is that this one is derived from the owner's own observation rather than from a theory
about the mechanism - and the two earlier attempts are still correct on their own merits.

### Theories killed by the owner's testing, in order (all reasonable, all wrong)

| theory | build | how it died |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stale viewport at the transition | v40.91 | ladder added; still broken |
| `display:none` destroying the layer | v40.94 | layers preserved; still broken |
| layout/visual viewport mismatch | — | `VV` == `win` == `scr`, boxes correct |
| clipping by `overflow:hidden` | — | `H`/`B` boxes are full-viewport |


## v40.97 — the canvas had no stacking position (attempt 5 at the mobile fullscreen overlays)

`canvas { display: block; cursor: none; }` was the WHOLE of the canvas's styling: **no `position`, no
`z-index`**. A static, in-flow element paints below every positioned overlay, so on paper the order
was always right. But a WebGL canvas is promoted to its own compositor layer, and the compositor then
has to promote whatever paints above it to preserve order ("overlap testing") - exactly the work
mobile compositors skip. The promoted canvas then composites OVER overlays that were never promoted.

That single mechanism accounts for every symptom at once, including the two that killed the earlier
theories:
- correct geometry and computed styles (v40.95: `VV`==`win`==`scr`, boxes full-viewport, every element
  `display:block`, `opacity 1`, correctly placed) - because nothing about the ELEMENT is wrong;
- **hit-testing still works** ("i can feel them working but can't see them") - hit-testing walks the
  DOM, compositing walks the layer tree, and only the latter is wrong;
- **they FLASH with `?pbhud` on** - each forced repaint briefly re-orders them.

Fix: `html.lss-touch canvas { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; z-index: 0; }`. Scoped to touch so
desktop is untouched, and deliberately no `inset`/`width`/`height` - `renderer.setSize` owns those.
**Verified geometrically inert**: with the class applied the canvas goes `static/zauto` -> `fixed/z0`
with the rect (1084x688@0,0), backing store and CSS size all unchanged; order becomes canvas 0 <
#touch-controls 11 < #ship-select-countdown 110.

### The four theories this replaces, all killed by the owner's testing

| theory | build | how it died |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stale viewport at the transition | v40.91 | settle ladder added; still broken |
| `display:none` destroying the layer | v40.94 | layers kept alive with `visibility`; still broken |
| layout vs visual viewport mismatch | — | `VV` == `win` == `scr`, boxes correct |
| missing paint invalidation | v40.96 | `void offsetHeight` flushes LAYOUT, not paint - and `_cdPaint`
  writes new text every beat (a real paint dirty) and the digits still did not appear |

⚠ v40.91, v40.94 and v40.96 are all still correct on their own merits and stay in. None of them was
this bug.

⚠ **If v40.97 also fails**, the remaining option is architectural rather than another CSS guess: draw
the touch controls and the countdown INTO the WebGL canvas (the HUD canvas path already exists -
`_hlRadar` blits into it), which sidesteps DOM compositing entirely on the device that cannot be
trusted to do it.


## v40.99 — IT WAS THE OVERLAY REHEARSAL. Found by bisect, after six theory-driven fixes missed.

Owner, after the v40.98 switchboard: *"https://lss.fractalreality.ca/?off=all made it work... it was
rehearse. That fixed it."*

`_prebakeOverlayRehearsal` (v40.34, grown in v40.45 and v40.58) shows ~37 transient overlays behind
the loading cover so their compositor pipelines exist before the player can see a first-use hitch. On
a desktop that buys a few milliseconds. **On a phone it exhausts the layer budget, and the overlays
the game actually needs - the touch controls and the countdown - are never composited again**: laid
out, styled visible, hit-testable, and simply not drawn.

⚠ It also cost the most exactly where it helped least. `flags.uiw` from the owner's own marks:
**1786 ms on one run and 12918 ms on another** (`worst` 1553-4340 ms) - seconds of load time on the
device that could least afford it, to avoid a hitch that is invisible next to losing the UI.

Fixed by gating it on `_fxSmallDevice()`. `?rehearse` forces it back for a desktop A/B; `?off=rehearse`
disables it everywhere. **Verified**: desktop still rehearses (37 overlays, 264 ms) and the countdown
runs 3-2-1-LAUNCH clean.

### ⚠ THE PROCESS LESSON, which matters more than the fix

**Six theory-driven fixes missed this**, each reasonable, each verified, each wrong:

| # | theory | build | how it died |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | stale viewport at the transition | v40.91 | settle ladder added; still broken |
| 2 | `display:none` destroying the layer | v40.94 | layers kept with `visibility`; still broken |
| 3 | layout vs visual viewport mismatch | — | `VV` == `win` == `scr`, boxes correct |
| 4 | clipping by `overflow:hidden` | — | `H`/`B` boxes full-viewport |
| 5 | missing paint invalidation | v40.96 | `void offsetHeight` flushes LAYOUT not paint, and `_cdPaint` writes new text every beat and still did not show |
| 6 | canvas stacking / overlap testing | v40.97 | explicit `z-index: 0`; still broken |

What ended it was **the owner's question**: *"why would it be css unless we changed something that
affects css? because it was working before"*. That reframed the problem from "which browser behaviour
explains this" to "which of OUR changes caused this" - and the answer was a switchboard (v40.98,
`?off=`) that reverts each post-40.44 change so one session bisects it, instead of one build per guess.

⚠ Note the switchboard proved its own worth twice: the arms that were NOT the cause (v40.91, v40.94,
v40.96, v40.97) are all still correct on their own merits and stay in, and `?off=all` also produced a
black screen behind the HUD - which is `vpdirty`/`cvsz` reverting the canvas handling, not a new bug.


## v41.00-41.12 — water displacement: the spray root, the sheet, and one undeclared variable

Owner: *"I don't really like the way the ship and weapons interact with the water... The way the water
displaces and splashes when objects move fast at angles, we need to fix. It would also drag with it
when it goes under water, and drag water droplets with it when it surfaces out of the water."*

### The physics, and where the old model was inverted

| what | source | what the code had |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spray-root speed `V·cot β` | Wagner (1932); the flat-plate impact measurements call it the *geometric intersection line velocity* | gated the whole splash on the VERTICAL speed alone |
| spray direction = free stream **reflected about the stagnation line** (swept-wing decomposition) | Savitsky & Morabito, *Origin and Characteristics of the Spray Patterns Generated by Planing Hulls*, JSPD 27(2):63-83 | an invented ±90° fan with a random forward lean |
| droplet speed **> 2×** the contact-line speed, rising with Fr | arXiv:1804.01068 | 0.16-0.60× — three to twelve times too slow |
| wake angle narrows as **U⁻¹** above Fr = U/√(gL) ≈ 0.5 | Rabaud & Moisy, *Ship Wakes: Kelvin or Mach Angle?*, PRL 110 214503 | a fixed offset with no angle in it at all |
| cavity elongates, **deep-seals at ~half its depth**, then a **Worthington jet** | Truscott/Epps/Belden, Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 46:355-378; Duclaux et al., JFM 591:1-19 | nothing |
| **~20° magic angle** minimises the speed to ricochet | Clanet, Hersen & Bocquet, *Nature* 427:29 | ships passed straight through |

⚠ **The old gate was not under-tuned at angle, it was inverted.** A ship crossing at 400 u/s on a 5°
path has Vn = 35, which scored **I = 0.036** — one droplet or none. Reality does the opposite: the
shallower the angle, the more violent the sheet, because as θ→0 the spray-root speed tends to
V/β_hull independent of the angle. Measured on the shipped model: **0.036 → 0.501** at 400 u/s / 5°,
and **0.099 → 0.729** at 900 u/s / 3°, with a vertical entry on a reference hull unchanged to 3 decimal
places (the spray root is normalised by the reference hull's tan β precisely so it cannot regress the
case that was already right).

### ⚠⚠ THE JELLO: every seed was ~20× past the display's own ceiling

Owner: *"something unrealistic about it... maybe looks too jello like when the boats and weapons hit it"*.

What you see is the displaced mesh, whose vertex shader is `disp = uRelief * tanh(h * uGain / uRelief)`
with uRelief 9 and uGain 95 — **96% saturated by h = 0.19**. Measured with `__waterProbe()` after a hard
entry on the pre-41.02 build:

| | peak h | saturated texels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v41.01 and every build before it | **3.60** | **70.6%** |
| v41.03+ | 0.53 | **0.7%** |

Seven of ten disturbed texels were a flat-topped 9-unit plateau, so a pistol shot, a ship at cruise and
a ship slammed in at full speed all produced the *same* rounded dome. `impactPeak` was 50; it is 0.135,
measured so a hard entry lands at 8.2 of the 9 units the display can show. A seed is also part
**impulse** now (`uSeedImpulse`) rather than a pure pluck — a pluck sets a displacement AND a matching
velocity and then lets go, which is a plucked membrane, which boings.

⚠ **And the first fix was the wrong instrument.** v41.02 put the recalibration in a GLOBAL scale at the
seed funnel, which cut the wake 14× along with the impacts — owner: *"now the water barely moves when
the ship touches it"*. The wake family never multiplied by `impactPeak` and was never broken. The owner
had localised the fault in their first sentence (*"when the boats and weapons HIT it"*) and I fixed it
somewhere else. **When a report localises a fault, fix it AT that location; a global knob is not a
cheaper version of a targeted fix, it is a different and worse change.**

⚠ `uSeedImpulse` 0.65 was then too much of a good thing: an impulse must integrate up over ~a quarter
wave period before it is visible, so at 340 u/s the crest arrived 27 units behind the hull and kept
growing after it had gone — owner: *"something lags behind when you move through it... like it's
sticky"*. 0.25 keeps the crater-and-radiate character without the lag.

### ⚠⚠⚠ `_beta` WAS NEVER DECLARED — four builds of silent total failure

v41.04 added two references to `_beta` inside `_swSpawnSplashV` while the deadrise was still computed
inline under a different name. **There is no `_beta` anywhere in the file.** Every call that got past
the intensity gate threw a ReferenceError before spawning a single droplet: the planing sheet, the
impact crown and every weapon plume, from 41.04 to 41.07. That is the whole of the owner's *"there's no
splash"* and *"it's incomplete"*.

⚠ **And it took the rest of the frame with it.** The planing emitter calls it bare inside
`_swRippleTick`, whose only caller wrapped it in `try { ... } catch (_) {}` — so on every frame the ship
was skimming, the throw unwound past the wake trough seeds, the crossing impacts, the ricochet,
`R.prevAbove = above` and the whole of `_swWetTick`, and was swallowed in silence. **That is also why
the ricochet never fired in any test**: `prevAbove` was not being updated on exactly the frames that
mattered. I spent an hour on that as a separate mystery.

Why nothing caught it: `node --check` parses, it does not resolve scopes, so an undeclared identifier
is a clean syntax tree. The console was clean because the exception never reached it. And my own
verification measured particle COUNTS and tanh saturation — numbers that stayed plausible while the
thing they described was not running.

**What found it: `window.__waterFX()`, the emitter census (v41.07).** One counter on each of the eleven
emitters, asking not *"is this the right amount"* but *"did this happen at all"*. It read
`plane: 68` calls against `sheet: 0, crown: 0` in a single line.

| | before 41.08 | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sheet droplets | **0** | 250 |
| crown droplets | **0** | 169 |
| ricochets | **0** | 4 |
| Worthington jet | — | fires |

The ripple tick's catch now records to `window.__water.tickErr` / `.tickErrN` and logs once, and the
census surfaces it. **A `catch (_) {}` around a per-frame system is a place where a total failure can
hide indefinitely.**

### The sheet (v41.09-41.12)

Owner: *"don't do two sheets... make the one sheet bend and warp and fractalize"* — which is also the
more honest physics. A spray sheet is one continuous film leaving the whole spray root:

- **BEND** — the root is a curved line and the direction the film leaves rotates along it (ψ is
  interpolated across the span), so the sheet wraps from one chine, around the keel contact, to the
  other. Every earlier version picked a side with a coin flip, which is why it read as a blob stuck to
  the hull.
- **WARP** — one travelling wave along the root, amplitude growing with distance out (the film is stiff
  at the root and unstable where it has thinned). Not per-droplet noise.
- **FRACTALIZE** — film → ligaments → droplets → finer droplets (Squire / Rayleigh-Plateau), so a parcel
  draws a breakup LEVEL from a geometric distribution and its size, scatter, reach and life all follow.

⚠ The reach is also what unsticks the spray from the hull: a parcel is placed ALONG the sheet at the
distance its level puts it, so the shape exists the instant it spawns. **v41.09 overdid it** — 2.75
beam-widths and a 0.15 size floor spread the same count over ~10× the volume and it read as nothing.
41.10 pulls the reach to ~1 beam-width, floors the cascade at 0.27 and doubles the parcels per burst.

v41.11 adds the **rooster tail** (its own transom emitter — there was none; what looked like an arc was
just bow parcels being left behind) and **crest dots**, the underwater-bubble look in air: small, bright,
low-gravity specks that hang off the crests we already know the positions of, plus the crest-break
scan's own peaks. Rooster height was tuned against screenshots: 1.0 read as a low haze, 2.5 as a wall,
**2.0** is a clean column that still falls as an arc.

### Knobs (all on `window.__water`)

`oblique` `plane` `entrain` `shed` `wxCap` · `seedScale` `impactPeak` `seedImpulse` `crater` ·
`trim` `waveG` `waveFrc` `jet` `jetDelay` `skip` `skipAngle` `skipSpeed` ·
`sheetBend` `sheetWarp` `sheetFrac` · `rooster` `dots` · `breakPool`

`seedScale = 1` + `impactPeak = 50` restores the pre-41.02 surface exactly, in two assignments.

### Instruments added

- **`window.__waterFX([reset])`** — the emitter census plus the live gate state. Any zero after a flight
  that should have triggered it is a dead gate, not a tuning problem.
- **`window.__waterProbe()`** — reads the heightfield back and reports what the display's tanh does with
  it. `satPct` is the number that matters; anything much above a few percent means the surface has lost
  its dynamic range and will read as jello however the seeds are shaped.
- **`window.__obliqueTest(V, deg)`** — the spray root, ψ, which spray family, the sheet's world speed as
  a multiple of ship speed, Fr and the wake angle, for any approach.
- **`window.__groundY(x,z)` / `window.__waterAt(x,z)`** — ⚠ three of this session's measurements were
  taken over dry land before these existed. The hub lakes are small (the one used here is ~1200 units
  across); never assume the spawn or the origin is water.


## v41.13-41.28 — the crest, and weapons that hit the water like the ship does

### ⚠⚠⚠ THE PROBE WAS READING A MATERIAL THAT IS NOT ON SCREEN, AND I QUOTED IT FOR TEN BUILDS

`window.__pw` (relief 9 / gain 95) belongs to `_swBuildHubWaterOverlay`, which **returns `null` on its
second line** — the mesh is never built and `__pw` is never created by the game. Every *"the crest is
pinned at 9 units"* reading came from constants belonging to a material that does not render.

The water you actually see is the mesh built around **L29900**:

```glsl
_hx  = h * uGain / uDispScale ;   disp = uDispScale * (_hx / (1 + |_hx|))
```

a rational sigmoid with a **180-unit** ceiling, live-tuned by `window.__water.disp` / `.gain`. The probe
now reads the live uniform off `game._hubWaterDispMat` (v41.13), and the stale comment that was the
source of the wrong premise is gone (v41.15).

### ⚠⚠ THE CEILING WAS NEVER THE CONSTRAINT — THE SLOPE WAS

`uDispScale` appears in the numerator too, so raising it alone does almost nothing. **Measured live:**

| change | crest at the hull |
| --- | --- |
| `uDispScale` 180 → 900 | 51 → 67 units |
| `uGain` 180 → 650 | 51 → 150+ units |

For these amplitudes it reduces to `disp ≈ h · uGain`. The heightfield was responding to speed properly
all along (h = 0.17 at 80 u/s → 1.22 at 500 u/s, a 7× range); the display was flattening it.

### ⚠⚠ ...BUT A FLAT GAIN WAS THE WRONG SHAPE, AND IT WAS THE v41.02 MISTAKE AGAIN

At `uGain` 650 the transfer function's knee (`h = D/G`) lands at **0.277**, inside the working band —
the measured near-hull crest is 0.41. Local slope collapses **565 → 106 → 23** across h = 0.02..1.2, so
h 0.41 gives 107 units and h 1.20 gives only 146: tripling the field buys 36% more crest. That is the
same compression that made every impact look identical before v41.03. And being a slope, it lifted
ambient leftovers from 8.6 units to **27.5** — permanent chop on untouched water.

**A crest-only expander does what a gain cannot.** Shape the height *before* the clip:

```glsl
hs = h * (1 + uCrestQ*|h|)          // uCrestQ 11, uGain 100, uDispScale 180
```

so h→0 is governed by `uGain` alone (calm water unchanged) and crests turn quadratic and outrun the
clip. Measured: ambient 5.1 (was 27.5), crest 100 at 330 u/s, 144 at h 0.8, 161 at h 1.2.

### ⚠⚠ THE WAKE VANISHED OVER WATER BECAUSE THE NORMAL DESCRIBED THE OLD SURFACE

Owner: *"the wake disappears when it's seen over top of water... if it's in front of a mountain or land
it can be seen"*. `(hL-hR)*uGain` is the correct normal only while `disp = h*uGain`, which stopped being
true when the expander went in — the real crest slope is ~2.5× what it reported. A 139-unit crest was
being *shaded* as a gentle ripple: normal near vertical, fresnel and specular identical to the flat
water beside it, reflecting the same sky. **A shape change has to be carried into the normal.** They
now difference the shaped displacements over the taps' real 4-unit separation.

And it never whitecapped: foam keyed on height alone (`vDisp > 0.47` to clear `uPeakLo` 0.32) while the
crest runs 0.41–0.70. **A whitecap is a steepness event** — real water breaks near slope 1/7 — and
nothing in the shader looked at slope. `peak = max(peak, steepF * uSteepFoam)` keeps the old height path
intact and adds the term that separates a wake crest from ambient swell.

⚠ I sized the steepness threshold from the PRE-expander geometry and 0.085 whitened the whole lake.
Bisected against screenshots: everything foams at 0.085, nothing at 0.65, the crest sits near **0.50**,
and it needs a strength cap (`uSteepFoam` 0.55) because foam mixes to 90% opaque and full strength
paints a wall.

### ⚠ `vDisp` IS NOT THE DISPLACEMENT

The fragment keys foam and spray off it (`uPeakLo`, the eml weights), so tying it to the geometry means
every height change silently re-tunes the foam — under `uGain` 650 foam started at h ≈ 0.13, i.e. on
ambient chop. It is a fixed, shape-independent measure of disturbance (`h/(1+|h|)`), so the crest knobs
can move freely.

### The rooster tail, and why the knob is not the height

There was **no stern emitter at all** — what looked like an arc behind the boat was bow-contact parcels
being left behind. `_swRooster` launches at 45–75° off the transom. ⚠ The apex is **not** proportional
to the knob: the particle integrator's per-frame drag eats the launch speed inside ~0.13 s, so height
goes as roughly `k^0.7`. Sampled peak height over a run: **k=2 → 78 units, k=5 → 147, k=8 → 304,
k=12 → 450**. Owner asked for 4×; 8.0 is the 3.9×. Reading it off the knob would have been out by 2×
in either direction.

### One sheet: bend, warp, fractalize (v41.09-41.10)

Owner: *"don't do two sheets... make the one sheet bend and warp and fractalize"*. BEND — ψ interpolated
across the spray root so the film wraps chine-to-chine. WARP — one travelling wave along the root,
amplitude growing with distance out. FRACTALIZE — a geometric breakup level drives size, scatter, reach
and life. ⚠ v41.09 reached 2.75 beam-widths with a 0.15 size floor: same droplet count over ~10× the
volume, and it read as nothing. 41.10 pulls the reach to ~1 beam-width and floors the cascade at 0.27.

### Weapons (v41.19-41.28)

⚠ **Coverage was never the problem.** All weapons already reached the water in v40.99; the look was the
problem. Two real defects:

1. **The seed was positive** — since v33.21 every round made the surface *bulge up* at the point of
   impact. A projectile punches a cavity and throws the displaced water as a rim around it. Same
   inversion v41.02 fixed for the hull, never carried across.
2. **Nine call sites, every radius and amplitude a LITERAL** (65/0.08, 78/0.09, 90/0.14, 110/0.12,
   140/0.07). A Gatling round and a railgun slug punched identical holes.

**The fix that mattered: weapons run `_swImpact`, the ship's own function** (owner: *"weapons hitting
the water should be the exact same as the ship, actually"*), with a footprint their own size and an
`ampK` scale. They get the crater+rim, the velocity gash, the bent/warped/fractal sheet, and on the way
out the shed sheet.

⚠ **The amplitude then comes from the FOOTPRINT, not from the yield's `A` term** —
`baseA ∝ fp.DRAFT = R*0.19`. Tuning `A`, which is what I did first, moved almost nothing. Against the
hull's own impact seed of **0.0806**:

| | before | after (R base 30→45, ampK 0.15→0.55) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gatling | 0.0049 (16× weaker than the ship) | **0.0271** |
| Blaster | 0.0097 | 0.0531 |
| Thermite | 0.0142 | **0.0783** (≈ a hull impact) |
| Railgun charged | 0.0279 | 0.1533 |

Also in: a **vent** (deferred collapse column, reusing `_swWorthingtonJet`) — ⚠ my first threshold
(0.055) was above *every weapon in the game*, so it would have been dead code; 0.009 splits Gatling/
Zapper (pock) from Blaster and up (collapse). An **exit plume** for firing up from below, which produced
literally nothing before because the emitter takes its intensity from the *downward* normal and the
helper forced that sign — ⚠ and I then gated it on `_swSubmerged`, the one condition it exists for.
A **projectile wake** (`_swWpnWake`) for anything skimming the surface, matching the hull's near-water
wake. And `_swBlast` for explosions: crater+rim above, dome+vent below, deferred column.

⚠ **A budget must thin an effect, not delete it.** Both weapon budgets were early returns, so once a
250 ms window filled every further hit produced a ripple and nothing visible — in a firefight, most of
them. They scale the burst with a floor now. The pool had the headroom all along: 218–385 live against
a cap of 4000.

### Knobs added

`disp` `gain` `crestQ` `foamSlope` `steepFoam` `normK` · `rooster` `dots` · `blast` `wpn` `vent`
`wpnWake` `wxCap` `wxSeedCap` `spdTail`

### Instruments

`__waterFX()` census · `__waterProbe()` (now reads the live uniform, reports `nearHull`) ·
`__obliqueTest()` · `__blastTest(size, dy)` · `__groundY` / `__waterAt`

## Water v41.31 - v41.65

### v41.31 - v41.47  (dots, bubbles, HUD, VR, draw distance)

- **41.31** second, finer/brighter layer of crest dots (`dotsFine`, a multiple of the coarse count).
- **41.32 - 41.39** the underwater bubble cloud becomes a FLOW field: a potential-flow dipole past the
  hull + viscous wake entrainment + shed vorticity (`flow` / `flowWake` / `flowSwirl`), bubbles born at
  the nose and recycled (`bubbleNose`), present only above a speed knee (`bubbleSpeed`), with
  projectiles and beams as extra sources (`flowProj`). Per-point `aSize` via `onBeforeCompile` -
  ⚠ that hook is what makes the material its own program; see the v41.65 warm note.
- **41.40** HUD: one ammo tick per ROUND (`_hlAmmoSegs`, subdivides past 40 so a tick is always a whole
  number of rounds), and the whole HUD's GRAPHICS go translucent while its TEXT stays at alpha 1
  (`_hlGA()`, `window.__hudAlpha`, default 0.72). Five gauge helpers assign their own alpha, so a
  blanket `globalAlpha` could not work - each assignment is multiplied instead.
- **41.41 - 41.43** VR: stasis and the tether root stop driving the view (`_vrHold`); the VR HUD
  defaults to 3x with a one-time migration (saved settings override defaults, so the new default alone
  was a no-op); full water becomes a VR OPTION (`_swVrLite()` / `input.vrWater`) instead of hard-off.
- **41.44 - 41.47** ripple draw distance. ⚠ The window was never the binding constraint -
  DAMPING was: at visc 0.9885 a ripple is down to 11% by 3000 units. 256 res / 8000 bounds AND visc
  0.9945 together. The crest-break readback moved to a centred 128x128 sub-rect so a wider sim costs it
  nothing, and the Reflector's `uRippleBounds` literal 4000 (only ever right by coincidence) was fixed.

### v41.48 - v41.65  (whitening, the spikes, and the reflection hunt)

**Whitening.** 41.48 found the height route to foam mathematically dead - `smoothstep(uPeakLo, 1.0,
vDisp)` where vDisp saturates at 0.5 - and gave it a reachable `uPeakHi`. 41.49 added the crest cap,
after 41.48's first cut gated it on SLOPE and fired on nothing (a crest apex is its flattest point:
the five tallest near-hull texels measured slope 0.013-0.073 against a 0.50 gate).

**41.49 the spikey triangles.** Seeds narrower than a texel (`Math.max(20, r)` vs 31.3 u) land on one
sample = the 2-texel Nyquist mode, which the v41.15 crest expander draws as a 130-unit needle;
`R.pending` caps at 8, hence "4 or 5". Floored at 1.5 texels of the live grid, area-corrected. The
wake got STRONGER (near-hull vDisp p90 0.133 -> 0.171, slope p90 0.294 -> 0.473) because the energy
now goes into travelling waves instead of a mode that does not propagate.

**41.53 - 41.56 the foam field.** Owner: "the white peaks should only be on the wake behind the ship
and weapons, not on all the waves/ripples". Height cannot separate them - the sim reflects waves off
shorelines, so the whole lake carries crest-amplitude ripples within seconds. Foam gets its own field
in the heightmap's unused `.z` channel: deposited where energy is injected, decaying in place, never
propagating. Every seed comes from a hull or a weapon, so that field IS the wake. It gates the crest
cap (41.53), the reflection matte (41.54) and the aerated albedo (41.55, its own much wider window).

**41.61 the faceted ripples.** The sheet is `PlaneGeometry(24576, 768, 768)` = 32.0 u/quad against a
31.3-unit texel - one vertex per texel. The facets were the NORMAL: its taps sat +/-2 world units,
inside one texel, and a LinearFilter heightmap has a piecewise-CONSTANT gradient, so every vertex got
its texel's constant normal and each triangle shaded flat. `uTapW` spans half a texel each side; the
normal formula was already parameterised by tap width, so it is free.

**41.58 the wings.** Every wake seed was placed off `fp.BEAM`/`fp.half`, and `_swShipFootprint` builds
those from the chassis BODY: `half` = 45 units on a ship whose bounding box is 317 across. A wing tip
159 units out could be underwater and touch nothing. Wing tips now get their own contact test at the
real half-span (`_swHullSpan()`), with the right vector off the ship's quaternion so roll carries in.

**41.63 THE REFLECTION.** ⚠⚠ `if (dot(reflTex, luma) < 0.04 && graze > 0.5) reflTex =
skyT;` - it asks "is this pixel dark?" when it means "did the sample land somewhere valid?", so it
punched pale sky through the DARK PARTS of any reflected hull or cliff, per pixel, at grazing angles.
That single line is "the texture is broken", "cut out to white", "the land cutting through the wake",
"all ships but slayer and puncture" (dark hulls trip it) and "only once you get close enough"
(graze > 0.5 = down near the water). Replaced by the condition it was proxying for: `ruv.w <= 0` or
the projected UV off the texture. 41.64 then removed the edge feather that fix introduced - a planar
mirror's UV space IS screen space, so feathering it drew a haze frame along the bottom of the screen.

**Dead ends kept for the record.** 41.50-41.52 (mirror parallax, tilt shear, `uReflPerturb` 0.6 -> 4.0)
and 41.54/41.57 (the hull water-exclusion) were all aimed at the reflection artefact and all missed it;
41.57 reverted the perturbation (at 4.0 the shear moved the sample 13% of the SCREEN) and 41.58 turned
the exclusion off by default (it flattened the near wake, which starts at the hull). The machinery
stays behind `window.__water.hullR` / `.reflPar` / `.reflWave`, armed by nothing.

**41.65 the warm.** `_warmDrawRoot(root)` with one argument returns before it draws. Three warms had
shipped dead - the bubble cloud, the bird/fish mesh, the Vortex core glow. `rt` now defaults to
`postFX.rtScene` with a one-time warning, the bubble warm moved from the COUNTDOWN into
`_prebakeGpuPrime` (seeded first, or `Box3` frames a point), and the flock's compile-only half-warm
became a real draw.

### Knobs added

`peakHi` `capLo` `capHi` `capStr` `capSteep` `capFreq` `capBright` `capFoamLo` `capFoamHi` ·
`matteLo` `matteHi` `foamMatte` `foamAlb` · `foamDecay` `seedFoam` `seedTexels` · `tapW` ·
`reflPar` `reflWave` `reflPerturb` `reflChop` `reflDevD` `reflDevN` · `refractMax` `murkMin`
`murkTint` · `hullR` `hullFade` `hullTop` · `debugTerm`

### Instruments

`__crestStat(radius)` - vDisp / slope / foam percentiles at the hull or out in the wake, replicating
the vertex shader exactly. Set every threshold against it; three have now been shipped outside their
own range. · `__mirrorDump()` - the planar mirror's render target into a canvas (proved the RT was
correct while the screen was not). · `window.__water.debugTerm = 1..8` - the water outputs ONE term
full-screen. · ⚠ Bisect the water by DETACHING it from the scene: `_swRippleTick` rewrites
`.visible` and the Reflector's `colorWrite` every frame, so hiding either proves nothing.

**41.65 / 41.66 the cleanup.** `_warmDrawRoot(root)` with one argument returns before it draws;
three warms had shipped dead (bubble cloud, bird/fish mesh, Vortex core glow). `rt` now defaults to
`postFX.rtScene` with a one-time warning, and the bubble warm moved from the countdown into
`_prebakeGpuPrime`. Then 41.66 backed out `uReflDevN` (1.6 -> 0) and trimmed `uFoamMatte`
(0.85 -> 0.35): both were built to fight the black-out guard, and with it fixed they only produced
the pale, low-contrast wash the owner reported as "still gotta fix the water here". ⚠ The
deviation fade keys on `1-N.y`, which ordinary ripples reach - it was never crest-only.

**41.67 - 41.74 the shoreline.** 41.67 low-passed the displacement to what the mesh can carry; 41.68
shrank the sheet for density and traded a seam for it; 41.69 removed that trade with a WARPED grid
(80% of the lines cover the inner +/-4000 at 13.0 u a quad, the rest stretch to 12288 - same 768^2
vertices, full reach); 41.70 snapped the sheet to its own lattice (it had been sliding a fraction of
a quad every frame - "when i hit p to freeze, the water goes back to normal") and moved the normal
to a per-fragment quantity (the owner had already isolated this: "3, 7 and 8 i don't see the
triangles" - the three isolator terms that do not read the surface shape); 41.71 capped the surface
GRADIENT at 0.9 (measured 1.5, a 56-degree face, against deep water's real limit of 1/7).
Then the actual cause: **41.72** the shoreline is a lossless wall and the wake was accumulating
against it (h = 1.41 measured against a +/-0.55 seed clamp), so the shallows absorb now; **41.73** the
water's alpha read only the near mask, so it was opaque past the ripple window's square edge - the
horizontal straight line; **41.74** the reflection UV clamp smeared an edge texel past the mirror -
the vertical straight line. ⚠ Live: `,`/`.` shore absorption, `;`/`'` viscosity, `[`/`]` maxSlope.

## FREE FLIGHT: EARTH — v46.76 notes (ad panels + streamed-patch hitches)

**Jump:** `_buildAdPanels()` · `_adPanelPlace(` · `_adFacadeClear(` · `function _leSlicer` · `function _leBreath` · `window.__earthTiles`

- **Ad panels stood 90° to their facades** (owner: "some of the ad signs go into buildings"). `_buildAdPanels` turned the edge direction by a quarter twice (`atan2 + π/2`, then `(cos, -sin)`), so every panel's normal ran ALONG its wall: a 15-35 m sign edge-on across the facade, half inside the tower. Measured on the 12 nearest panels over Toronto: panel·wall normal 0.00, centre on the wall plane. Now: outward normal from the ring's winding (+ a point-in-poly probe), `_adFacadeClear` probes the panel face against the collision grid at the panel's height (own footprint included), a blocked facade slides along the wall → narrows → rotates to the next longest edge → is skipped; a facade that already carries a panel is skipped (outline+part pairs used to stack two panels 2 m apart). `stats.adsPlace` tallies it. Verified: 39/40 panels dot 1.00 at the 1.2 m inset.
- **Streamed-patch hitches (?pbhud):** 467/542 ms frames blamed `earth:stream` = `_loadBuildings` with `prefetchedWays` never awaits, so its whole tail (suppression, taper anchors, 142-408 ms of extrusion, merges, ads) ran inside the streaming tick's late backfill; the 50-90 ms long tasks with no blame were the DEM ring's post-load passes and the 144 imagery tile draws running as the LAST tile's `onload` continuation (named by a `long-animation-frame` PerformanceObserver's `scripts[].invoker`). Every such loop now runs on `_leSlicer()` (6 ms slices while playing, 40 behind the curtain, `window.__earthSliceMs`), `_leBreath()` sits between `_build` stages, `_bldBusy` serialises the two backfill callers. Same harness: worst frame 133 → 58 ms, gaps ≥100 ms 7 → 0.
- **Texture upload:** `flipY` on the 3072² CanvasTexture was a CPU flip of 36 MB inside texImage2D (28-37 ms vs 15.7 ms measured live); `_makeTexture` sets `flipY = false` and `_uvIn` runs v top-down (roof-colour lookup follows). Far rings draw their tiles straight into the capped canvas instead of compositing at 3072² and downscaling.
- ⚠ **The 2D canvas defers its draws**: after slicing the tile loop the imagery frames were still 40-52 ms because the 144 queued `drawImage`s rasterised (and decoded their JPEGs) at the first READ, in one burst the slice clock never saw. `ctx.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1)` every 16 tiles flushes the work into the loop. Shipped result over a downtown teleport rebuild (7 dense patches): worst frame 50 ms, no gap ≥ 100 ms.
- Left as is: the region cache read (`IDBRequest.onsuccess`, 50-96 ms once per ~8 km, a 10 MB structured clone), ~15 ms per patch for the texture's first draw.
- **`strip.py` stamped `lss.js?v=0` on every build** (single-quote regex vs double-quoted source) while `_headers` caches `/lss.js` immutable for a year — fixed; the tag is `lss.js?v=<LSS_BUILD>` now.
- **(v46.76, same day) Building coverage:** the region query's core is `nearRadius + 0.5` cells wide, the near ring `nearRadius`, so one cell of drift left the ring's far edge with the wide query's towers only, and "has a `_bldList`" counted as "has its city" so it stayed that way. `_bldCoreKeys` / `__bldComplete` / `_clearBuildings()` + the re-fetch on any cell change (guarded by `_bldRegionPending`) fix it. **Water finder:** flood into `<= level + 0.5` from the seed set, then an R = 8 texel closing (`window.__earthWaterClose`); harbour uncarved-at-surface 17% → 1.2%. **Skybox leak:** `cyberpunk.jpg` stayed visible under a live weather dome after the `_wxDispose → _wxInit` cycle the water build causes; `_skyDomeRefresh` now gates on `_WX.on && _WX.dome` and the Earth tick self-heals it. **Earth ad ground:** `uAdsGFade` (0.01, 0.03) per Earth material (`window.__ads.earthGfadeOut/In`). Open: a faint far-field marbling on daylight water at altitude (exclusion list in memory).
- **(v46.77)** Earth traffic tows ad banners (`_elSpawn` → `_hcAttachBanner`, every third hull; `_elDetach` disposes them). **Ripple window rim = sponge, not wall:** `_SW_RIPPLE_FRAG`'s `nh *= edg` (a 6%-wide hard zero on the new height only) reflected every wake off the window's square; replaced by a quadratic damping of both height fields over the outer 18% (`uSpongeW/uSpongeK`, `window.__water.spongeW/spongeK`). `__waterProbe()` now reports `bandEdge/bandInner` RMS; measured rim energy 5% of interior with the sponge vs 56% with the wall.
- **(v46.77)** ripple `viscosity` 0.9945 → 0.9970 (wake half-life ~2 → ~4 s). Wake angle unchanged: Rabaud–Moisy narrowing (v41.04) gives a 20° V at the hull's on-water 350 u/s (Fr 0.97); `window.__water.waveFrc = 1.3` holds Kelvin's 39° up to cruise. The sim's wave speed is ~956 u/s, so only projectiles make a Mach cone.
- **(v46.77) The 39° wake:** the ripple sim is non-dispersive, so a hull only leaves a stationary V by outrunning its waves (a Mach cone at asin(c/v)); while a hull lays a wake the sim's wave speed now follows it, c = v·sin 19.47° (`window.__water.kelvinSin`, floor `waveCMin`, `waveC2` pins). Player stamps in the wake step, entities in `_swEntityWaterTick` on the wake condition, reader in `_swRippleTick` (1 s freshness, eased 2/s, back to 0.26 off the water). Measured: 117 u/s under a 350 u/s hull. Cost: skimming projectiles cone narrow while a hull is on the water.
- **(v46.77) Wake look:** whitecaps in `_SW_RIPPLE_FRAG` (foam from crest slope, `uBreakK/uBreakThr`, `window.__water.breakK/breakThr`) so the cone's arms whiten and the interior stays dark; `_SW_RIPPLE_RES` 512 on desktop (a `let`, set in `_swRippleInit`, `window.__water.res`); entity wake seeds every 0.12 s; entity spray default 0.6.

- **(v46.78)** **Hull-shaped water displacement.** `_swHullSilhouette` renders the player hull's underside from below (hull frame, 64x64 `MeshDepthMaterial`) and `_SW_RIPPLE_FRAG` turns it into a moving pressure patch: hollow (`-immersion*k`), rim (displaced water stood up around the body) and a closing tail (the transom section shrinking to a point `tailLen` behind = the towed hollow crashing together on the centreline); the change between poses is CARRIED (both height fields shift, `uHullKick` keeps a fraction as a pluck) - the pluck form left a filled mound behind the ship. `_swCrashSpray` = inward-flying droplets at the apex. Knobs `window.__water.hullPress/hullRim/hullTail/hullTailK/hullKick/hullFoam/hullCrest/crashSpray/hullRes/hullRedo`; debug `__hullP`, `__hullSilDump()`, `__seedLog()` (with `__seedLogOn`). **Entity-wake runaway fixed:** a wild leviathan's wake seeds (heft 8.5, no cap, no depth term) drove the field to -48 (a saturated plateau dragged behind the ship); `_swEntityWaterTick` now caps a seed at `entAmpCap` 0.08 and fades it with depth, and the sim clamps `|h| <= uHClamp` (1.2, `hClamp`) as a safety net.
- **(v46.78 cont.)** Rooster tail spawns at the closing hollow's apex when the hull patch is on (`roosterAt`); hull SKIM pull so a hovering hull still carves a shallow V (`skimDepth`/`skimH`, fades 2.5 drafts up); tail heights linear in hull speed via `_swTailUp` (`tailH`, 0.12 u of height per u/s) for both `_swRooster` and `_swCrashSpray`.
- **(v46.79)** **Stray "<ability> ACTIVE" banner on a ship change.** The banner is `Overlays.abilityFlash`, reachable only through `activateAbility`, which was gated on dead/warmup/cooldown and nothing else. Traced live (banner wrapped to log its stack): the strays were ability presses / hold-prime releases landing around the swap, and the keyboard dispatcher never checked for a menu. Now `_abilitiesBlockedByUi()` (settings, picker, lobby, `select`/`matchEnd`) and `_abilitySwapLocked()` (0.6 s of game time after `commitLoadout`) gate `activateAbility` and both `abilityInput*` entry points; the commit also drops hold primes, releases the bound ability keys and re-syncs the gamepad edge state.

- **(v46.80) EVERY WEAPON'S WATER IMPACT HAD BEEN RUNNING AT 1/20.** Owner: *"the laser type weapons aren't making ripples in the water ... blaster's weapons and abilities ... vortex main weapon, syphon main weapon, and rail gun is a tiny ripple ... i don't even think the rockets are making ripple when they hit the water (just their explosion does, and they cause wake)"*. `_swImpact` is the one "something hit the water" function and `_swWpnCross` has routed every weapon through it since v41.27 — but its `baseA` multiplied by **`window.__water.wake`**, which ships at **0.05**. `wake` is not a global water scale, it is the **hull's** calibration (the v44.82 note: the hull's wake seeds run ~20× past the display's ceiling), so recalibrating the hull silently divided every weapon by twenty and the v41.28 weapon table — measured and shipped at `wake = 1` — has been a twentieth of itself ever since. **The report's ORDERING is the proof:** the four hitscan mains rank exactly by damage (85 / 240 / 380 / 1000) and only the railgun's 0.0018 was big enough to see, while the two paths the owner says DO work — `_swBlast` (0.55, the seed clamp) and `_swWpnWake` — are precisely the two that never multiplied by `wake`. Fix is at the **caller**, not the knob: `_swImpact(..., ampK, wakeK)`, `wakeK` defaulting to `__water.wake` so every hull-family caller is bit-for-bit unchanged, and `_swWpnCross` passing 1. Measured, Gatling straight down into the hub lake with `wake` still 0.05: crater seed **−0.0008 → −0.0150** at radius 194.
- **(v46.80) Multiplayer parity, two gaps.** The peer-tracer hook passed a flat yield of **120 for every weapon** (no damage travels with `fire_tracer`), so a peer's railgun and Gatling punched identical holes — it now resolves `LOADOUTS[evt.lo].weapon` (the loadout was already in the event, read a few lines below for the railgun spiral) and takes the same `mainK` trim the local main gun does. And the peer **Vortex Laser ability had no water hook at all**: the local one has had `'vLaser'` at yield 2400 since v41.78, while the `effect_spawn / vortex_laser_beam` branch that draws the same beam for everyone else had none — the game's biggest beam reaching the lake only as its own thin tracer. ⚠ Stipple keys are **per peer** now (`'peerTracer' + fromPeerId`); a shared key meant six players firing over the lake laid one sparse trail between them, the same defect v41.37 fixed for projectiles.
- **(v46.80) `viscosity` 0.9970 → 0.9940 — the jello the fix exposed.** Owner immediately after: *"when i shoot it, it bobs up and down too much for too long ... the surface looks like jello"*. **Neither change was wrong alone.** v46.77 raised viscosity judged on a WAKE (one hull laying a smooth train, half-life 2.1 → 3.9 s); v46.80 gave weapons back their 20×, so the lake is now struck properly twenty times a second into a field that holds energy twice as long. The measurement that names it: one burst then nothing driving it — the PEAK fell 0.236 → 0.101 over 3 s while **`hRms` sat flat at ~0.015**, i.e. energy spreading rather than dissipating. `visc^60` is the per-second factor: 0.9970 → ×0.835/s (3.85 s half-life), **0.9940 → ×0.697/s (1.92 s)**, owner: *"you just fixed it"*. ⚠ One constant damps every wavelength equally, so **the ship's wake shortens with the ringing** — taken knowingly. The fix that separates them, if the wake is later judged too short, is viscous damping by **curvature** (`nh += uViscK * (lapH - lapV)`, ν∇² on the velocity term — real dissipation goes as ν·k², so chop dies fast and a long wake train does not), and it costs **no extra texture fetches**: `_SW_RIPPLE_FRAG` already reads the four neighbours as `vec4` and discards the `.y` channel the second Laplacian needs.
- **(v46.80) THE BODY-SHAPED PATCH FOR MONSTERS.** Owner: *"Monsters have a huge bowl shape around them on the surface of the water, it doesn't match their body, we fixed the ships, let's fix the monsters to be the same"* — v46.78's one open item. The bowl was literal: `_swEntityWaterTick` lays ONE round seed of radius `fp.BEAM * 1.25` (a 462-unit circle on a size-672 leviathan). `_hImm` / `_hullP` now take their silhouette, rect and y-range as **arguments** rather than reading one fixed uniform set, so one implementation serves the hull plus two entity slots (`uEntTex0/1`, `uEntA[2]`…`uEntT[2]`); `_swHullSilhouette(mesh, slot)` caches per slot; selection runs **before** the budget-gated round-robin loop (deciding mid-rotation gives a body a patch one frame and a bowl the next) and scores `BEAM / distance`. A/B on one monster, `__water.entPress` 1 vs 0: **hMin −0.157 vs −1.200** and hRms 0.0029 vs 0.0995 — and **−1.200 is exactly `uHClamp`**, so the old bowl was pinned against the v46.78 safety clamp as a flat-bottomed saturated plateau, which is what "huge bowl" meant. ⚠ A fully-submerged body **keeps** the round seed: `_hImm` saturates to the whole body height at every texel and the patch is a bowl again, just an expensive one. ⚠ The hollow is capped in **sim units** (`entHollow` 0.22, ~2× the ship's) — the 1/170 constant is calibrated on a hull's ~20-unit draft and the display's expander `h(1+11|h|)` is quadratic, so the same constant on 140 units of wading leviathan asks for h = 0.82.
- **⚠⚠⚠ (v46.80) THREE SKINNED-MESH TRAPS in `_swHullSilhouette` — every ship in this game is rigid, so none had ever fired.** (a) a leviathan has **no `userData.bboxSize` child** (that marker is written by `buildModelShipMesh`; a monster's mesh is a plain Group holding a scaled GLTF clone), so the ship-hull lookup returned null and the body silently kept its round seed; fall back to the mesh itself. (b) **a skinned body has no shape in its geometry** — cloning `o.geometry` into a plain `THREE.Mesh` draws the BIND POSE and `geometry.boundingBox` measures it: **8.9 × 5.3 × 11.2 world units for a size-780 animal** (bind pose authored near unit scale, group scale 458.8, the mesh's own world scale 4.43 — the BONES carry the rest). Clone as a `SkinnedMesh` sharing the skeleton and take the box from `SkinnedMesh.computeBoundingBox()` (r165 has it; plain `Mesh` does not), which walks vertices through their bones into the mesh's local space; ⚠ never call `bind()` without an explicit matrix, it runs `skeleton.calculateInverses()` and rewrites the LIVE animal's bind pose. (c) **a skinned mesh cannot be posed by writing its `matrixWorld`** — three recomputes `bindMatrixInverse` from that same matrix inside `SkinnedMesh.updateMatrixWorld` every render, exactly cancelling the frame transform, so the body lands at its real world position and the frame-space ortho camera is aimed at the origin 30 km away and **the RT comes back EMPTY with a perfectly correct rect and box** (the box is CPU-side and never goes near the render). Fix: draw in **world space** (`matrixWorld = identity` makes `bindMatrixInverse` identity and the shader's skinned vertex IS the world-space one; a rigid mesh gets there with `o.matrixWorld`) and put `frame` on the **camera** (`cam.matrixWorld = frame · localCam`; ⚠ clear `matrixWorldNeedsUpdate`, which `updateMatrix()` raises). **Provably a no-op for ships:** old `modelView = inv(localCam)·(inv·o.mW)`, new `= inv(frame·localCam)·o.mW = inv(localCam)·inv·o.mW`.
- **⚠⚠ (v46.80) AN EMPTY SILHOUETTE MUST FAIL BACK TO THE ROUND SEED, NOT TO NOTHING.** Trap (c) produced a well-formed record whose texture was blank, and the consequence was **worse than the bug it was fixing** — a patched body skips its round seed, so the monster stopped disturbing the water at all (owner: *"they aren't jiggling the water right now"*). Nothing threw and nothing logged; the only way to see it was to dump the texture by hand. `_swHullSilhouette` now reads the RT back once per body and counts drawn texels (`window.__water.silMinFill` 0.004, `_swRipple.silFill`); below that it returns `null`, the caller's `_ok` stays false and the body keeps the seed it has always had. Healthy readings are `fill` 0.13–0.14.
- **(v46.80) Instruments.** `window.__entP` (both entity slots: id, k, wl, tailLen, rimR, sil.fill/beam/len) · `window.__hullSilDump(cols, slot)` — slot 1/2 are the entity slots, **all dots = nothing drawn** · `window.__water.entPress` 0/1 for a live patch-vs-bowl A/B with no reload · `window.__water.visc` is read every tick, so decay is live-tunable. ⚠ **`__waterProbe()` returns all zeros when there is no water in the ripple window** (the mask early-outs every texel) — that means "you are not over water", not "the sim is broken"; I read it the wrong way once. ⚠ To ask "what is driving the surface", reset `__waterFX(true)` and run `__seedLogOn = true` / `__seedLog()` for a few seconds and bin the seeds by **distance from the player** — a 5 s census is what showed the ringing was `blast` 8 / `blastColumn` 5 / `wpnCross` 1, i.e. not weapons at all.

## v46.82 — RACE CIRCUITS: the Earth Circuit and the Overworld Circuit

**Jump:** `const RACE_CIRCUIT = {` (the module, right after `_raceFinishUnlocked`) · `MAP_DATA.race_earth` / `MAP_DATA.race_overworld` · `function _lssHubWorld` · `function _raceCircuitBotWaypoint` · `function _raceCircuitNetTick` · `window.__race`

Owner: *"races in custom locations... a circuit through whatever place you choose to drop into... capture the rings in order. A ring will appear when it is next to capture... then the final objective (the champion field). The positions of the rings/circuit will be identical for everyone... rings appear low and between buildings, with a ring up high every now and then. Rings will always appear on the mini map... open up the overworld in race mode, with a massive circuit through all the cities."* And, mid-build: *"bots in race mode, first priority should be the rings, sub task is to kill the enemy."*

- **Shape.** `game.raceCircuit` = one shared lap (`rings[{x,y,z,d,tx,tz,high}]`, `start`, `fin`) and every racer carries its own cursor (`_raceIdx` on `player`, each `Bot`, each `NetworkPlayer`). All the `RaceRing` objects are built at once (they share the pinned cyanring program) but `RaceRing.update` draws only ring[cursor] for the local pilot and captures for them alone; a capture advances the cursor. Past the last ring `_raceCircuitAnyCleared` opens `_raceFinishUnlocked`, the stasis owner spawns the champion field at `fin`, and `_raceCanClaim` refuses the field to anyone still on the lap (proxy bots never claim; a peer's ship claims on what its `race_prog` said).
- **Two maps.** `race_earth` (type gmaps + `stream: true` + `circuit: 'earth'`): the streamed Earth world at the DROP location (the panel relabels to RACE CIRCUIT and hides the finish box; `gmaps_user` keeps the old start→finish race). 12 gates on a wobbly 0.8–1.06 km loop; low gates 36–62 m up, high every 4th at roof+110–190 m. `race_overworld` (`Object.assign({}, hub_overworld, {circuit:'overworld'})`): 7 cities × 3 gates + 7 high transit gates = 28. **`_lssHubWorld()`** replaces `LSS.MODE === 'freeflight'` at the 8 world gates the hub needs (zone morph, hub clipmap, `nonSpawnRooms`, basin/hub clouds, gas, stream budget, `_lssFlightArena`); `_raceCircuitOverworldBuild` runs in `buildRoomGraphLevel` after `initSandwichTerrain` and builds all six sector cities through `_owEnsureSites`/`_owBuild`; `_owRaceFrame` keeps them lit and sun-shaded and nothing else (no carriers, fleets or boss - `_owFrame` stays free-flight only).
- **Placement** (`_rcPlaceRing`): a golden-angle spiral of 28 candidates around the route vertex; the nearest whose clearance from every building rising above the ring's BOTTOM exceeds ring radius + margin wins (Earth reads the patch `_cgrid` polygons in local metres; the overworld reads the city `hash` OBBs); nothing clears → climb 14 m/120 u steps; roof fallback always clears. Measured Toronto: low gates 38–58 m AGL with the tallest roof 74–220 m ABOVE them, high gates 64–99 m over the roofs.
- **⭐⭐⭐ Who decides.** The stasis owner generates (Earth: at the end of `_lssGmapsBuildLevel`, polling up to 14 s for the centre patch's buildings; overworld: synchronously in the build) and decrees `race_circuit` at 1.5 Hz until every peer acks (`race_circuit_ack`); a peer without a lap asks with `race_circuit_req` every 2 s; racers broadcast `race_prog` on each capture. The Earth curtain (`hideLoadingOverlay`) holds for the lap too (`_noCircuit`). The v43.24 rule, no pairwise arbitration.
- **⚠⚠ THREE THINGS THAT BROKE, all measured on the pane:** (1) `_lssGmapsApplyTerrainFollow` (the point-to-point race's shifter, on `_lssGmapsRefinePivot`'s 1 s timer) slid the finish room, the start grid, the pilot AND every bot 2,024 units down into the city while the gates stayed put - it now returns for circuits. (2) **THE RACE STUCK-DETECTOR COLLISION, older than this build:** the v32.71 race-waypoint detector held `game.time` in `this._stuckT` / a Vector3 in `this._stuckPos` - the SAME fields v41.93's `_unstickTick` uses as a seconds accumulator and a sample point. With a waypoint set, `_unstickTick` read `expect = speed × 125 s` on every sample, judged every race bot stuck and re-fired its escape forever (targetDir lerped to the escape at dt×4, beating the fork's dt×2): the roster orbited at full speed and never reached a gate. Renamed to `_rsWpPos`/`_rsWpT`; **this fixes Pole Position and the Shifting Run's bots too.** (3) Five cleared bots contesting a 50-unit finish dot shoved every holder out before the 0.5 s charge (CLAIM BROKEN on repeat, no round end): a circuit finish's `holdRadius` is 240 (`StasisField` ctor) and cleared bots take the v41.99 escort ring around a friendly holder.
- **Bots** (`_raceCircuitBotWaypoint`, the first branch of the race block in `Bot.update`): the next gate, approached from IN FRONT along its axis and FROM ABOVE (the approach point climbs 0.6 × distance up to 900 u - every placed gate has a clear column over it, a street-height approach point is behind a tower from most bearings; measured: a bot wedged on a hub podium at 20 u/s until this); the goal never sits below `ground under the bot + 170` (the terrain hover pad zeroed vel.y and bots crawled at 5–60 u/s down the lakeshore slope); a 760 u obstacle ray turns the goal up, then to either side, HELD 0.5 s; a stuck escape (speed < 70 for 1.2 s) goes up with a velocity kick. Bots capture at 0.62 × d (pilots 0.45). Dead racers come back after 4 s at the last gate they took, cursor intact (pilot via `respawnPlayer`, bots re-dealt in the same seat - the assault pattern); the round-end wipe rule is off for circuits. Rings first, guns opportunistic: the waypoint owns steering every frame, fire is the normal in-front-in-range path. Measured Earth lap: the roster clears in ~100 s; the overworld hub's three gates in ~35 s.
- **HUD / radar.** `#race-hud` (GATE n / N · distance · ▲ HIGH; CIRCUIT CLEAR · TAKE THE FINISH) pinned under `#round-info`; the radar draws the whole lap as a faint polyline, taken gates dim, the NEXT gate pulsing and edge-arrowed off the disc, the finish gold once clear; range 5,200 (Earth) / 14,000 (overworld). `window.__race.info()/rings()/skip()/tp(i)/regen()`.
- **Known / left as is:** the ship cruises on its own in the hub-race flight model, so an unattended pilot drifts through gates; the 3000 HP champion shell still seals the finish (existing race rule); `_raceCircuitOnLocalCapture` pushes the cursor one past N on a repeated skip (harmless, every test is `>= N`).

### v46.83 — race circuits, round two (owner's playtest notes)

**Jump:** `function _raceFinishExposed` · `function _raceRespawnPuff` · `function _raceGateLib` · `RaceRing._buildGateMesh` · `function _raceCircuitAuthority` · `window.__race.kill/killBot/expose`

- **Respawn where you died, 1.5 s, in a puff of smoke** (owner). `_raceCircuitRespawnTick` latches the death point on the first dead frame (`game._raceDeathPos`, `bot._raceDeathPos`); the pilot comes back through `respawnPlayer` behind the `game._raceRespawnInPlace` latch (a round-reset respawn keeps its spawn pick), our bots as a fresh hull in the same seat at that point; `_raceRespawnPuff` = a dozen pale cloud bursts + a light + `phase_dash`. Cursor intact. Measured: pilot back 42 u from the death point, bot seat re-dealt with its gate count.
- **The finish EXPOSED = no respawns** (owner: "if you die when the champion field is exposed, then you don't get to respawn"). `_raceFinishExposed()` = field alive and its shell down - the codebase's own word ("destroy the shell to expose the field"). The dead stay dead (NO RESPAWN banner) and the classic fleet-wipe ending returns for that phase, so a wiped fleet loses. Measured: sealed → a killed bot respawned; exposed → the bot and the pilot stayed dead, wiping fleet B ended the round 1-0.
- **Gates wear the endless Aegis bolt** (owner: "i just like the look of the powerup over the ring, and looks omni directional"). `_raceGateLib` is `_lssEndlessBoltSlot`'s exact recipe (octahedron core, fireball/plasma FX shells, glow sprite, three god-ray shafts) built once; `RaceRing({gate:true})` instances it at `diameter / 300` and animates it like `_aegis` (flicker, counter-rotating shells, precessing rays, a 12 u bob). It still acts as a ring: the capture is the sphere test. ⚠ Shared library: a gate's `destroy()` removes its group and disposes nothing. Capture cue = `rearm_reset` (the bolt's own) + its `fireball_cyan` flash.
- **⭐⭐⭐ The lap authority is the peer LONGEST IN THE ROOM**, not `amStasisOwner` (owner: "i saw someone capture my point, and it disappeared... it should be individual"). Gates are per client - a peer flying through yours cannot hide it - but the stasis-owner rule sorts random ids, so a drop-in joiner could win the lap, decree its own copy and make the host adopt it mid-race: gates cleared, cursor back to 1. `_raceCircuitAuthority` is v44.61's election with the `unknown` guard (keep what you hold); the authority never adopts; an identical lap (same kind, seed, ring count - the deterministic overworld) is re-tagged with nobody moved or reset.
- **The line to the next gate** (owner, second overworld city: "couldn't find the next ring, the line to the next one didn't appear on the map"): the radar now draws a dashed guide from the ship to the next gate, clamped at the rim when it is off the disc (the lap polyline only joined on-disc gates), the rim arrow gets a ring, and the HUD carries the bearing off the nose and a climb/dive cue: `GATE 3 / 28 · 540 M · 20° ▶ DOWN`. Measured: 40/40 sampled radar pixels cyan along the guide vs 6/40 on a control bearing; off-disc at 30 km the guide reaches the rim and the HUD reads `◀ 90°`, `▲` once faced.
