### v47.78-47.83 - the Spire's heavy hulls get to the fight: the right slab, the clear column, a lattice, and a brake

Owner, watching elimination on The Spire: *"just slayer had found me, and his friends didn't join in
the battle"*, *"the third bot never found me"*, *"he came for me in the end"*.

**Jump:** `THE SPIRE, PART 2` (above `_arenaNavAlignY`) · `THE SPIRE, PART 3` (above `_AL_DIRS`) ·
`function _arenaNavBlocked` · `function _arenaNavAlignY` · `_arenaLocalUpdate` · `_arenaLatTick` ·
`function _arenaEnsureLattice` · `function _arenaLatSearchStep` · `this._latCap` ·
`window.__arenaPath` · `window.__arenaPathReport` · `window.__arenaLatReport`

- **⭐⭐⭐ THE FRIENDS ARE THE HEAVY HULLS, AND THE SPIRE IS A MAZE FOR THEM.** BLASTER and PYRO are
  DREADNOUGHTs: hullLength 140, acceleration 500, top speed 250, drag 400 - c* (the clearance a hull
  needs to make ANY headway, v36.61's containment-stall note) is **139 u, against 68 for SLAYER**.
  `__spireArena.at` sampled on a polar grid, three heights per storey: **only 33-59% of each storey
  has 139 u of clearance** (the crown worst, 33-42%), against 69-84% at 68 u. Stalagmites reach
  ~690 u into the 634 u pit, stalactites hang 450 u under every slab and ~520 more from the cap.
- **⭐⭐⭐ MEASURE WHERE THEY WEDGE BEFORE CHOOSING THE TOOL.** The brief blamed same-storey pursuit.
  Every stuck escape logged with position, clearance and goal (two 60 s trials) said: **28 of 33 were
  the v36.61 SLAB ROUTER**, 27 in its ALIGN phase at clearance 139-163 (pressed at the hull's very
  limit); 5 were same-storey chases. Three causes, fixed in **v47.78**:
  - **⚠ THE WRONG SLAB (`_arenaNavBlocked`).** It returned the FIRST SOLID crossing between bot and
    goal - so when the goal line threaded a hole in the NEAREST slab somewhere far off, that slab was
    skipped and the bot was handed a throat one or two storeys up. **A PYRO in the PIT was routed at
    slab 1 and 2 throats for 36 s, pressing into slab 0's underside.** And the 148 u ring counted as a
    hole for a hull needing 139 u on every side. Now: the slab adjacent to the bot's storey, blocked
    unless the crossing sits `minClr` deep inside a hole.
  - **⚠ THE ALIGN ALTITUDE (`_arenaNavAlignY`).** ALIGN held the bot `lip` (150 u) under the slab -
    exactly where the stalactites hang. They only root where the slab is SOLID, so the column under a
    hole is clear: line up at the clearest height in it (9 samples), then THROUGH climbs.
  - **⚠ NOTHING STEERED AROUND ANYTHING (`_arenaLocalUpdate`).** A local planner: sphere-trace the
    field with c* + pad; when the line to the goal (or the router's ALIGN point) is not flyable, take
    the open heading nearest the goal for 0.55 s. Out of line-of-sight combat only.
- **⭐⭐ v47.78 ENDED THE WEDGING AND BROUGHT NOBODY.** Stuck escapes per 75 s trial fell from 21-25
  to 0-5 - and no DREADNOUGHT arrived: BLASTER circled the pit for 60 s at the right slab-0 throat,
  and SLAYER got SLOWER (13.7 / 19.5 s vs 6.5-8.2). **A local planner avoids what is in front of it;
  the pit is a maze, and a maze needs a path.** "Fewer stuck escapes" was never the goal - arrivals are.
- **⭐⭐⭐ v47.79 - THE LATTICE.** A clearance lattice over the whole arena, built ONCE per arena in a
  worker from the SAME `_ARENA_FIELD_SRC` string the collision and the mesh use, cached by the arena
  params like the mesh (round 2+ instant - verified: ready during round 2's countdown, same build; a
  non-arena build disposes it). Nodes every 160 u, each nudged to the clearest of 7 samples in its
  cell; edges to the 26 neighbours carrying the MIN clearance sampled along them. Slab holes, the
  helix and the spike forest are all just clearance, so ONE graph covers storeys and slab crossings.
  **8,928 live nodes, 75,035 edges, 5.3 s in the worker, ready before the countdown ended.** Main
  thread: hull-aware weighted A*, wide passages preferred, followed with a visibility look-ahead (skip
  to the furthest of the next 6 nodes the hull can fly to from where it IS). Until it lands, and
  whenever it has no path, the v47.78 router + planner steer. **First series: 12 of 12 bots arrived,
  DREADNOUGHTs 8 of 8, median ~35 s.**
- **⭐⭐ v47.80-47.82 - THE SHAFT TRAP, A WRONG TURN, AND THE BRAKE.** One spot kept eating DREADNOUGHTs:
  under slab 2's 128-degree shaft, three trials running. v47.80 blamed the path follower's 110 u
  "arrived" radius and halved it, and single-node bans on a stall - and arrivals went from ~35 s to
  ~60 s (A* just took the next node up the same shaft). v47.81 sampled every edge exactly where it
  crosses a slab face/midplane and made a stall ban a 220 u REGION. Still stuck there - so the column
  itself got measured: **bottleneck 192 u at y 1100, 235 u through the approach - wide open.** The
  wedge was HANDLING: bots have no throttle (full thrust on the nose, a speed clamp, drag), so a
  DREADNOUGHT turning up into a vertical column at 250 u/s carries ~80 u on drag plus ~100 u of heading
  lag, and the part of the column with 139 u of clearance is ~96 u across. **v47.82 brakes into sharp
  turns** (`_latCap`: 0.3 of top speed at a 125-degree turn, the nose swinging twice as fast while the
  lattice owns it), restores 110 u on gentle turns (55 u only before a sharp one), and moves the bans
  from a Map to a typed array (Map lookups inside A* had pushed the worst plan from 2.2 to 5.9 ms).
- **⭐⭐ v47.83 - A CAP, NOT AN AVERAGE.** Plans ran to completion inside one frame: worst 1.9-3.0 ms,
  about one a second across a squad - a dropped frame on a 144 Hz display whenever one lands on a busy
  frame. The search is now RESUMABLE: one in flight across all bots, at most 1 ms a frame, its bot
  flying its old path meanwhile.
- **RESULT - Spire, player parked in `spawn_a` (the crown), enemy hand BLASTER + PYRO (DREADNOUGHT)
  + SLAYER, bots healed each tick, time each bot first SEES the player itself, 75 s cap:**

  | build | trials | bots that arrived | DREADNOUGHT arrivals | SLAYER first sighting | stuck escapes / trial | worst planning frame |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | v47.77 (legacy, `__arenaPath.on = false`) | 4 | 6 / 12 | 2 / 8 (66.2, 69.1 s) | 5.8 - 24.5 s | 20 - 25 | - |
  | v47.78 (router fixes + local planner) | 2 | 2 / 6 | 0 / 4 | 13.7, 19.5 s | 0 - 5 | - |
  | v47.79 (+ lattice) | 4 | 12 / 12 | 8 / 8, 32.3 - 56.6 s | 5.7 - 7.6 s | 0 - 7 | 2.2 ms |
  | **v47.83 (final)** | 4 | **12 / 12** | **8 / 8, 33.7 - 38.1 s** | **5.4 - 5.7 s** | **0 - 1** | **1.3 ms** |

### v47.84 - race round 2: the pilot spawned at the world origin

Owner: *"In race mode, round 2, i spawned in a different location than the start."*

**Jump:** `function _raceCircuitHandOver` · `function _raceCircuitTrackBuild` (the v47.84 note) · the empty-pool guard at the top of `function _raceCircuitPlaceAll`

- **⭐⭐⭐ THE MECHANISM, three pieces that are each fine alone.** (1) `buildRoomGraphLevel` sets `game.corridorPoints = []`, calls `_raceCircuitTrackBuild(level, rooms)` right after `_buildRaceGraph`, and only THEN samples the new level's corridor points. (2) v47.10 made that track build call `_raceCircuitOnArrive()`, which runs `_raceCircuitPlaceAll()` whenever the round is not yet live - so it drew a spawn from the EMPTY pool, and `getValidSpawnPoint` answers an empty pool with `new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0)`. (3) `_raceCircuitPlaceAll` latches its pick through `_spawnPickSet`, and the v45.04 latch is exactly what the round's next `respawnPlayer()` consumes ahead of a fresh draw. Round 1 hid it: `buildWorld` re-picks and re-latches after the build. Round 2+ has no re-pick - `_rrReset` -> `respawnPlayer()` took the origin.
- **MEASURED, 47.83, solo, the Shifting Run:** round 1 spawned 74 u from `start_a1`; round 2 went live with the pilot at **(0, 0, -15), 10,174 u from the nearest start room**, all five bots on the new grid (the Shifting Run re-rolls its axis every round, so the origin is mid-course). **After (47.84):** round 2 169 u from `start_a1`; round 3 (reached by the owner winning round 2 with a gamepad) 123 u from `start_a2`; rings = poleRings both rounds; zero console errors. Owner: *"fixed confirmed and working"*.
- **Why it read as intermittent:** swapping ships in the between-rounds picker runs `commitLoadout`'s midMatch fork, which re-picks from the (by then real) pool. Keep your ship and you got the origin.
- **The fix:** `_raceCircuitOnArrive` is split. `_raceCircuitHandOver()` = drop the old lap's gate meshes + zero every cursor; the track build calls only that. `_raceCircuitOnArrive()` (the net/decree paths: Earth and overworld adopts, where `_raceCircuitInstall` has just filled the pool with the start grid) still places. Belt: `_raceCircuitPlaceAll` now returns with `[race] place-all skipped: no spawn pool yet` on an empty `corridorPoints` rather than latch the origin.
- **⚠⚠ DO NOT MOVE THE PLACE-ALL BELOW THE CORRIDOR SAMPLING.** In a room the whole build runs inside `withSeededRandom` (which swaps `Math.random`), and `getValidSpawnPoint` draws a DIFFERENT number of randoms per client - own team, and bots only on the bot authority - so any draw inside the build shifts the shared stream `spawnDynamicObjects` / `spawnOrganics` read next and the peers' worlds diverge. From an empty pool it drew none, which is the only reason this bug never desynced a room as well. Placement belongs to the build's CALLERS, after the build: `buildWorld` (round 1), `_rrReset` -> `respawnPlayer` + `spawnBots` (round 2+), `commitLoadout`'s midMatch fork (a ship swap).
- **⚠ GENERAL TRAP: `getValidSpawnPoint` on an empty pool is (0,0,0), silently, and `_spawnPickSet` makes any bad pick STICK for one respawn.** Anything that places a ship from inside `buildRoomGraphLevel` (before the corridor sampling), or before an async gmaps build has published its pool, gets the origin. The v46.89 Custom Location re-pick in `_lssGmapsBuildLevel` exists for the same reason.
- **Tell:** a pilot at or near (0, y, 0) at the start of a round, with the bots on the grid. `__race.info()` shows nothing wrong - the lap itself is fine.
- **Not exercised this session:** the Earth and Overworld circuits' round 2 (different path: `_raceCircuitEarthKick` / `_raceCircuitOverworldBuild` install the grid into the pool before anything places; read as correct, not measured) and Pole Position (same `circuit: 'track'` path as the Shifting Run, so covered by construction).

### v47.85-47.91 - race bots: the finish they would not break, the race line, hoop gates, the 4x Shifting Run

Owner: *"they are not very good from getting to point a to point b, because they are very distracted by fighting each other"*, then *"they are all hanging out at the champion field and none of them are breaking the barrier around it"*.

**Jump:** `const _isBreaker =` (the v47.85 race branch in the Bot fire block) · `const RACE_LINE = {` · `function _rcLineBuild` · `function _rcLineWaypoint` · `function _raceGateAxis` · `hoopGeo` (in `_raceGateLib`) · `const PER = ` / `window.__shiftRunPer` (in `_lssGenRaceTrack`) · `game._levelSpan` · the v47.90 box test in `_stRouteAt`

- **⭐⭐⭐ (v47.85) THE FINISH: A RACE HAS NO ESCORTS.** The shell-fire rule in the Bot fire block is ASSAULT's v41.93 breaker/escort split - even ids break, odd ids only take the shell with no rival inside `_OBJ_BREAK` (1,500). Race ids are 1,2,3 (fleet B) and 10,11 (fleet A), so whenever the first bots across the line were odd, the finish was all escorts; a finish always has a rival within 1,500, so they circled the standoff ring shooting each other and the shell only fell when their crossfire crossed it. **MEASURED (three odd-id bots cleared inside the finish room, pilot 20 km away): 47.84 = ONE deliberate shell shot in 15 s (it died to spill: SLAYER pellets 726, PYRO thermite 540, bot-owned projectiles 1,633); 47.85 = 42 deliberate shots, all three contributing, zero ship shots while the shell stood, broken 6.6 s after it spawned.** Rule: in race, a racer that may claim (`_raceCanClaim`) is always a breaker; one still lapping never aims at the shell. Unforced round after: cleared 28.4 -> broken 38.8 -> held 42.6 -> retaken 45.2 -> captured ~50 s.
- **⭐⭐⭐ (v47.86) THE LAP WAS NEVER THE FIGHTING - A NO-FIRE A/B SAID SO.** `__rh` harness with `_mayFight` forced false on the same seed: the gaps stayed. A 10 Hz trace of every bot found (1) **NEAR MISSES** - in most 4-10 s gaps the bot flew through the gate room 5-60 u OUTSIDE the capture sphere (0.62 d) and looped back; a 39-degree gate at 900 u/s is a ~1,600 u turning circle for a 500-acceleration hull on ~1,200 u legs (heavy hulls physically could not make it; PUNCTURE, 1,200, lapped clean at ~1.8 s a gate); (2) **OUTSIDE THE TUBE** - `chooseRaceWaypointTo` aims at the next room CENTRE from wherever the bot is (median 300-650 u off a 260 u tube; SYPHON wedged at 1 u/s for 6.4 s). Fix = the RACE LINE: pure pursuit on the tunnel centreline (speed x 0.7 lookahead, clamped to the gate centre) + a speed cap into and out of every sharp vertex, `v = sqrt(acc x 0.7 x roomR x 1.6 / angle)` (bots have no throttle - the Spire `_latCap` lesson). Stamped per frame (`_rcCap`/`_rcCapAt`), applied beside `_latCap`; a braking bot does not dash. **Same seeds, same hand (PYRO/BLASTER/TRACKER vs SYPHON/VORTEX), three rounds: mean lap 44.5 -> 32.6 s (-27%), slowest per round 53.1 -> 36.8 s.** Knobs `window.__raceLine = false` (47.85 exactly), `window.__raceLineK` (the table, live); counters `__raceLineN` / `__raceCapN`. Legs are ROOM PATHS by BFS over `game.raceGraph` (so they chain through the v47.90 bend rooms); leg 0 starts at the room where the start lanes meet (Pole Position's is one room, so it stays on the BFS).
- **(v47.87-47.89) HOOP GATES** (owner: *"make the race check points into tauruses, instead of spheres, but the same texture/shaders - don't let this affect the aegis orbs in endless"*). Same three layers on the same materials, as `TorusGeometry` in a sub-group that UNDOES the 4x findability scale: the core tube's inner edge sits on the pilot's capture sphere (`captureK x 300 + 12` in gate units), so **the hole is the checkpoint**. Shells spin in-plane (a tumble would tilt the hoop), the core flicker is a quarter of the orb's (a full one breathes the hole by a third). Faces `_raceGateAxis`: the bisector of the way in and out; **gate 1 faces the grid outright** (the bisector left it 38 deg off from the pilot's lane - measured; now 3 deg). Endless is untouched by construction: its bolts come from `run._boltLib`, and `_makeFXMaterial` returns a fresh material per call. Knobs `window.__raceGateHoop = false` (the orb), `window.__raceHoopGlow` (centre glow, 1 = as signed off). Owner: *"nice"*. The ring banner on a track now says "through the hoop" (it said "between the buildings", the Earth line).
- **⭐⭐ (v47.90-47.91) THE SHIFTING RUN AT 4x, A GATE EVERY FOURTH ROOM** (owner: *"make the rings... about the distance of every 4 rings how they currently are... let's make the distance 4x longer"*). Laid exactly as before - one room per ~1,300 u, the same per-room side/height walk and clamps - over 440-560 SU, and only every 4th room is a gate; the rest are `bend` rooms (plain caverns). **Bends are ROOMS, not extra tunnel points,** so every tunnel stays a straight room-to-room link (the one shape `chooseRaceWaypointTo` is right about) and the race graph stays a chain. Seed 3074246773: 18,274 -> 73,097 u, 56 rooms (4 start + 39 bends + 12 gates + finish), race line 13/13 legs. Three consequences handled: (1) **the arena box** - `_lssFlightArena` now returns at least `(game._levelSpan + 3000) / 0.8` (span stamped by `buildRoomGraphLevel`; the player's soft push starts at 0.8x) - every classic arena is unchanged; (2) **`_stRouteAt` loops EVERY room and tunnel per collision query / sdfNormal tap / raycast step** - it now skips anything whose box grown by `r + CLEAR_SOFT` misses the point, which is EXACT (an element only counts through `e > o` and e is 0 past r + soft; cylinder boxes cached as `_mnx.._mxz`, nothing mutates cylinder endpoints); (3) **rock clusters** - 2-3 per room would have tripled them onto the racing line; a bend gets one, out at 0.5-0.65 r. `window.__shiftRunPer` (build-time, 1 = the v46.84 course byte-for-byte, same draws in the same order; a LOCAL knob - peers must agree). **Frame time, same seed, parked pilot, 25 s: PER=1 p50/p95/p99 7.0/14.0/14.1 ms, 8 frames >16.7; PER=4 7.0/14.0/14.2 ms, 24 >16.7** (one run each; the streamer was still filling - 121 chunks vs 294). Unforced lap: first bot clear ~73 s after FIGHT, shell broken 7 s later, captured at +15 s.
- **⚠ TERRAIN IS NOT THE COST OF A LONGER TRACK.** A round build bakes a fixed 5x5 chunk core and the streamer keeps ~120-300 chunks around the ship regardless of the course length (both arms read 293-294 resident at one point) - the per-frame cost that scales with length is the route carve query, above.
- **⚠ `sed -i` IN GIT BASH REWRITES CRLF TO LF.** One `sed -i` on the LSS_BUILD line turned all 146,670 lines of index-working.html to LF (git's autocrlf hides it from the diff). Bump with the Edit tool or Python bytes.
- **Open:** gates still lost 5-8 s each for VORTEX twice in one lap on the line; the Earth / Overworld circuits keep their own from-above approach (untouched); the bots' `botCaptureK` 0.62 is wider than the hoop's hole (0.45 d + tube) - a bot can take a gate through the rim.

### v47.92-47.93 - PUNCTURE tether traps: shoot your way out (only the one holding you), and fainter

Owner: *"we should be able to shoot/destroy puncture tether traps (only if we are caught in them)... but let's also make them less visible, with more transparency"*.

**Jump:** `function _tetherShotProbe` · `function _tetherTakeShot` · `function _tetherShatter` · `const TETHER_ALPHA` · `const TETHER_SHOT` · `window.__tetherProbe` · the `_tetherShotProbe` blocks in `fireHitscan` / `fireSpread` · the projectile intake at the top of the tether dressing in `updateWorldEffects`

- **The trap is a worldEffect, not an entity - no gun could ever hit it.** It was NOT enrolled in `game.monsters` (~40 loops read that: every AoE, the bots, the monster net sync, the tether's own monster scan). It joins the **obstacle slot** that `fireHitscan` and `fireSpread` already use for "the nearest solid thing on this line" (dynamic objects, leviathans): a proxy with the same `takeDamage(dmg) -> dealt` contract, so the slot stops the shot there, credits it and shows the hit marker - and the railgun's pierce branch still strikes it. Pilot **projectiles** (PYRO, TRACKER, ability rockets) are taken in the trap's own per-frame branch: any `owner === 'player'` round with damage inside `hitR` is spent on it (silent despawn - the main projectile loop sweeps `!alive`).
- **Only the trap holding the LOCAL pilot is a candidate** (`_tetherHoldsMe`: triggered, `rootTarget === player`, not shot down). You cannot hit a trap you are not in; a trap holding a bot, or nobody, is untouchable exactly as before. Bots cannot shoot their way out (not asked for - the owner's own traps would get weaker).
- **Broken = free:** `playerRootTimer` drops to the longest OTHER tether still holding you (tethers are its only writer), the trap is swept like an expiry (timer 0), and an `effect_destroy` for its netId clears it on every peer (the sweep only broadcasts for the OWNER, and the victim is not). 1,200 HP (~0.5-1.6 s of a main gun), 70 u hit sphere - `window.__tetherShot = { hp, hitR }`. MEASURED VORTEX: 1200 -> 820 -> 440 -> 60 -> gone in ~0.8 s, root 3.1 s -> 0.
- **⚠⚠ THE SAME-FRAME RE-CATCH (v47.93).** `_tetherShatter` clears `triggered`, but the sweep that removes the trap is at the BOTTOM of the updateWorldEffects loop, after the tether's three trigger scans - so a victim still inside the 250 u radius was caught AGAIN in the same frame and re-rooted for 4 s by a trap that was then deleted (measured: root back to 3.9 s with no trap). All three scans now skip `_shotDown`. **And the tether dressing uses a local `_tethGone` flag, never `continue`: the removal is at the bottom of that loop body, so a `continue` would strand a dead trap in the list forever.**
- **Fainter:** a LayeredFX material has no global opacity - alpha is `uLayerAlpha[i]` x pattern, normal blending - so each trap's OWN two materials (fresh per trap via `_makeFXMaterial`, disposed not pooled by the sweep) get their layer alphas scaled from a stored base: **idle 0.35, caught 0.7** (`window.__tetherAlpha = { idle, caught }`; 1 = the old look), read every frame. The idle crackle is ~4x rarer (0.22-0.42 s, was 0.05-0.10) and thinner (0.6); once it has caught someone it crackles at the old rate and the tether arc to the victim is unchanged - it is the thing you now need to find and shoot. A hit flares the core (uIntensity 3.0 for 0.12 s).
- Probe: `__tetherProbe.drop(160)` lays an enemy tether off your nose (catches at once, radius 250); `__tetherProbe.list()`.
- **(v47.94) ...AND THE ABILITIES** (owner, cycling every ship in Exhibition against `__tetherProbe` traps: *"laser shot no"*, *"fire shield no"*, *"none of the fire stuff"*, *"thermite launcher yes worked"*). Anything that flies a `Projectile` was already covered (rockets, Cluster Missile, Stun Bolt, the rocket cores); the rest resolve their OWN loops, so each asks one of three shapes about the tether holding you, with the damage it just dealt: `_tetherHitSeg` (Laser + the Mega Laser core, which runs through the same block; YOUR Flame Chain / Mega Flame Chain walls at their 150 u reach; every Charge Shot pellet and the long-range slug), `_tetherHitSphere` (YOUR ignited Explosive Gas; YOUR armed Plasma Mine trips on it and detonates into it), `_tetherHitCone` (Fire Shield - its own cone and falloff). Energy Syphon competes on its single-target ray (`_tetherShotProbe`) - 800, no lifesteal off a trap. No damage by design: the shields, Afterburner, Range Mode, Inner Spark, Sonar Pulse, AI Assist.
- **⭐⭐ (v47.94) A TELEPORT ESCAPE IS AN ESCAPE** (owner: *"teleport is supposed to escape it... but it escapes only to be recaptured lol"*). v35.63 re-arms the trap on purpose and v46.90 made the hop real - but the hop goes along the NOSE and you were caught flying INTO the trap, so a 400 u hop from ~200 u short lands ~200 u past it, inside the 250 u radius, and the re-armed trap took you the next frame. The break-out now sets `_escaped`: that trap ignores the local pilot until they are clear of its radius (+40 u), and still catches anyone else (and you, if you fly back in).
- **(v47.95) ITS OWN SOUND** (owner: *"it sounds too much like cluster missile explosions"*). The break played `firework_pop` - the Cluster Missile's bomblet crackle - and every plain `spawnExplosion` adds the `'explosion'` boom (hits on the trap too, through the hitscan obstacle slot). New recipe `tether_snap` in `DEFAULT_SOUND_LIBRARY` (PUNCTURE: a 40 ms highpass crack, a rising 1.3-2 kHz ping, a falling 440/660 -> 110/165 twang and a 330 -> 55 Hz saw zap, no sub thump); every tether flash is `spawnExplosion(..., { mini: true })` (the picture, no shockwave, no boom). Tune it in `sound_lab.html` -> Sync with Game HTML -> open index-working.html -> Load to editor. Owner: *"nice"*.

### v47.97-48.00 - THE REPLAY SYSTEM: a data recorder, the FINAL KILL cam, and the replay studio

Owner: *"it wouldn't even bog the frame rate like the other recorder does... because it works a completely different way... we could do call of duty style round end replays, like the final kill... we could allow to save recordings, and have a replay studio to shift perspectives and watch from something like ghost mode... and we could use it as a dev tool... i think elimination mode is the place to start this"*.

**Jump:** `const _RPL = {` (top of the boot scope - TDZ, see below) · `// ⭐⭐⭐ (v47.97) THE REPLAY RECORDER` (the whole module, just above `function renderFrame`) · `(function _rplInstallTaps` (every wrapper, beside the playerDie / respawnPlayer wrappers) · `if (_RPL.studio) {` in gameLoop (the paused-match fork, right after `pollGamepad()`) and in pollGamepad (the pad hand-off, after the LB/RB reads) · the `_RPL.kc && game.state !== 'roundEnd'` guard at the top of gameLoop · `window.__replay`

- **⭐⭐⭐ IT RECORDS WHAT THIS CLIENT DRAWS, not what crosses the wire** - so solo against bots (no packets at all) records exactly like a room. Per round (from FIGHT): every ship's DRAWN pose (`mesh.position` / `mesh.quaternion`, 20 Hz, stride `t,x,y,z,qx,qy,qz,qw,alive`) keyed `me` / `b<seat>` / `n<peerId>`; every projectile's position (drawn back as a bare core); every call to the PURE visual spawners (tracer, railgun spiral, pellets, FX burst, lightning, sparks, hit fire, hull burst, muzzle flash, shield hit, explosion) and the two sound calls; every death with its killer. A replay RE-CALLS the spawners - they carry no damage, no net, no sound of their own (audited). `Projectile`, the world effects and die() carry gameplay and are never re-run. 37 s of a 6-ship round = ~3,800 events + ~4,000 pose samples; the recorder is 20 Hz array pushes, and the studio holds 143 fps in the pane.
- **⭐⭐ THE TAPS RECORD THE OUTERMOST CALL ONLY (`_RPL.nest`).** spawnExplosion spawns FX bursts and lightning of its own (PUNCTURE's muzzle flash a bolt): recording the inner calls too would draw everything twice on replay. Sounds nest separately (`sndNest`) - an explosion's boom IS recorded, and replayed explosions come back `mini` (picture only) so the boom plays once, from the recording.
- **THE FINAL KILL CAM** (classic only): at FIGHT a new recording starts; at the whistle, the last kill within 3 s of the end is replayed from a chase camera behind the killer (look target turns onto the victim, slow motion around the kill, the boom walked in until `worldSDF` says open air; no killer known -> a slow orbit of the victim). It BORROWS the live hulls (a dead bot keeps its detached mesh until the next spawnBots pools it) and poses them in renderFrame after `_orbitCamApply` - the last writer. Letterbox + `FINAL KILL` + names in class colours; any key / click / fire / pad A-B skips; **R or pad Y opens the studio at that kill.** Knobs `window.__killcam = { on, lead, tail, slowA, slowB, slowK, delay }`.
- **⚠⚠ (v47.99) IT MUST FIT THE 5 s ROUND-END WINDOW.** Played through, the defaults take ~4.85 s of real time (2.4 s at 1x, 0.7 s of replay at 0.35x = 2 s, a 0.45 s hold) and only ~4.65 s is left after the 0.35 s delay. At warmup the between-rounds picker owns the screen and **gameLoop stops calling renderFrame, which is what drives the kill cam** - an overrun froze the letterbox under the picker, and its hand-back could then restore a hull the next round's spawnBots had already re-dealt. So: the lead-in gives up whatever does not fit (`lead` in `_rplKcStart`, never below 1 s - measured 1.99 s, the cam ended 0.36 s before the picker); a guard at the TOP of gameLoop ends any kill cam once the state leaves roundEnd/playing; and `_rplKcEnd` skips a mesh whose `userData.bot` changed hands.
- **⭐⭐⭐ THE STUDIO (v47.98) PAUSES THE MATCH - the settings contract.** `if (settingsOpen) return` in gameLoop is what Esc already does to a solo match; the studio is the same early return one branch up, but it draws at full rate: `_rplStudioLoop` runs the cinematic fork's ambience list (water, critters, city, weather), the replay's blasts at the studio's speed (`_rplTimeK`), then renderFrame, whose `_rplFrame` poses everything. **SOLO ONLY** (`_rplStudioCan`: not in a room, not XR, classic, state playing/roundEnd, no fly-in). It poses its OWN hulls ("puppets": `createShipMesh` per actor's loadout, from the bot pool when one is parked) - a library round's bots were pooled and re-dealt long ago - and hides the paused match's hulls and in-flight shots (re-hidden every frame, restored exactly on close).
- **Views:** CHASE (behind the followed ship; drag / right stick swings it, wheel / left-stick-Y zooms), COCKPIT (the pilot's eye: hull quaternion x a half-turn about Y, since a hull's nose is +Z and a camera looks down -Z; that ship's puppet is hidden), ORBIT (world-fixed az/el, drag / wheel), GHOST (free fly: WASD + QE + drag, Shift fast, wheel = speed; pad sticks + LB/RB). Timeline with every kill marked (click / drag to scrub), 0.1x-4x, kill-to-kill jumps (lands `lead` before the kill, behind the killer), a name label over every ship, a kill toast as each death replays. Sounds only between 0.5x and 2x.
- **⭐⭐ WHILE IT IS OPEN IT OWNS THE INPUT.** Keys: a window CAPTURE listener swallows everything but F-keys (the game's keyboard is document-level, so it never sees them - `[` `]` are `cycleHubShip` and Q is an ability, both reachable otherwise). Pointer: over the world = drag/wheel for the camera, swallowed; over the panel = its controls, and **the panel root stops bubbling** because the game's document `mousedown` (fire latch + pointer-lock grab) only spares `<button>`s and the timeline is a div. Pad: a hook in pollGamepad AFTER the stick/button reads and BEFORE any menu or gameplay edge runs `_rplStudioPad` and returns (A play, B exit, X view, Y next kill, LB/RB ship, LT/RT analog scrub, D-pad seek / speed, Start library, Back hide UI); every *Prev latch stays fresh, so nothing fires on a stale edge at hand-back. The press that opened it is seeded into `gpPrev` (the kill cam's Y would otherwise read as "next kill"). A pointer lock that lands late (closeSettings requests one) is dropped on `pointerlockchange`.
- **⭐⭐⭐ THE CLOCKS (v47.99).** (1) The round clocks are WALL-CLOCK anchored (`_anchorTimer` / `_tickTimer` - an alt-tab cannot stretch a round), so they ran on under the studio: **the first test closed it 52 s later and the 80 s round ended on the very next frame, by timeout.** Close now moves every `game.*TimerAnchorMs` forward by the pause (solo only, so no peer disagrees). (2) The RECORDING clock is `_rplNow()` = game time minus `R.pa` (the studio's accumulated pauses), frozen at the open moment while the studio is up - otherwise a round you paused to watch records every ship parked mid-air for as long as you watched, and a live round's length grows while you look at it. (3) A round the CLOCK ended (`R.endBy === 'timer'`, read on the transition frame) has no final kill - the HP tiebreak decided it. ⚠ **Esc settings has the same wall-clock hole** (a long pause in settings ends the round on close); not changed here.
- **THE LIBRARY:** the session's last 8 rounds live in `_RPL.lib` (the one in progress too). SAVE -> IndexedDB `lss-replays` (`meta` for the list, `rec` for the whole round); EXPORT -> `lss_replay_<map>_r<N>_<stamp>.json` (the same object - the dev tool: hand it to Claude as a bug report); IMPORT FILE reads one back. **A recording plays only on the level it was flown on** (`R.sig` = `_rplLevelSig()`: the map key, plus round + seed for procedural / pillar maps that re-roll per round) - ships and shots are data, the level is not. Anything else lists as OTHER MAP. `__replay.studio(id, { force: true })` plays anywhere (dev).
- **Entry points:** the kill cam's REPLAY STUDIO button (R / pad Y); Esc -> Settings -> **REPLAY STUDIO** (injected by wrappers on `openSettings` and `buildSettingsPage` - both call orders exist); `__replay.studio()`.
- **⚠ TDZ:** `_RPL` is declared at the top of the boot scope (beside `LSS_BUILD`) because the taps are read by spawners that can run during boot (the prebakes spawn effects to warm them). v39.02 rule.
- **Probe / dev:** `__replay.info()`, `.log()` (the lifecycle in one line each: states, the final-kill verdict, why a kill cam did or did not start, the studio's open/close - **read this first when a kill cam "just didn't play"**), `.lib()`, `.saved()`, `.save()`, `.dump()` (export), `.kc()` (force the kill cam from the last kill), `.studio()`, `.st()`, `.close()`.
- **Not in a replay (v1):** world effects (tethers, stasis traps, fire clouds, gas), shields and other hull-attached ability visuals, engine trails, damage smoke; the level's own state (champion shell, dynamic objects). A projectile is a bare core. Verified in the pane on hourglass (solo, desktop + the 375 px mobile preset: nothing overflows); the pad mapping has NOT been exercised on hardware.

### v48.12-48.13 - the Vortex Shield holds longer under fire; Broken Simulation gets its water

Owner: *"vortex needs a vortex shield buff... it seems to get depleted really fast when absorbing damage, so let's slow down that depletion a little so it can absorb a bit more damage before draining so fast"*. And: *"water is broken in the spire and in the diamond (and all diamond themed maps)"* - asked what they saw: *"they both had something that looks like water surface, just a flat horizontal plane, but it doesn't do anything/react like water"*, then *"spire doesn't need water"*.

**Jump:** `window.__vortexShield` (the hold loop in updateAbilities) · `function _swCavernWaterWanted` · the `T.biome === 'brokensim'` branch of `_swApplyAtmosphere`

- **(v48.12) VORTEX SHIELD DRAIN UNDER FIRE.** Holding it drains `drain` 250/s times an absorb amp that builds from the damage absorbed in the last `ampWindow` 0.45 s. The amp used to hit its 2.0x ceiling at 150 damage, so heavy fire burned the whole 1000 pool (1400 at Aegis rank 8) in 2.0 s. Now the ceiling is 1.5x, reached at 250 damage, and a stray hit costs 1.05x (was 1.1x): heavy fire drains 375/s = 2.67 s, a third longer. The idle hold (250/s) and regen (150/s) are unchanged; bots have no vortex energy model, so this is the pilot's shield only. Knob `window.__vortexShield = { drain, ampMax, ampMinHit, ampFull, ampWindow }`. Built and node-checked, not measured live.
- **⭐⭐ (v48.13) THE DEAD WATER WAS THE FLOOR.** Broken Simulation (The Diamond `gyre`, the campaign's `camp_brokensim`, any map on the Broken Simulation theme, and an endless deep whose roulette rolls `brokensim` via `_biomeOverride` - that last one untested) had NO water object. v38.16 flooded every cavern's basins to YFLOOR + 16 % of the ground relief but left this biome dry on theme alone ("a failing simulation with an open sky gets none"), so its valleys bottom out in the terrain's bare flat floor - ray-cast on The Diamond: -640 at every sample across the spawn basin - and a smooth, flat, horizontal plane that never moves reads as dead water. The theme reason is reversed: `_swCavernWaterWanted` now excludes only `mossy` (the hub has its own sea) and the brokensim branch builds the cavern water instead of disposing it. MEASURED on The Diamond: WL -420.8 (-600 + 0.16 x 1120), mirror + 1.18M-tri displaced sheet up, ripple sim live (17.7k active texels from the bots' wakes before anything was touched; a skim moved the displacement range from -63..+76 to -84..+52), and it mirrors the purple glitch sky. Only ~5 % of the map floods: the central basin and some shallow edge pools. Owner, flying it: *"the water is working"*. `window.__cavernWater = { on: false }` still dries every cavern.
- **The Spire stays dry.** It is an arena with no sandwich terrain; the flat plane in its pit is the lava floor, and the owner: "spire doesn't need water".
- **Open (general cavern water, not new here):** the displaced sheet flips to `DoubleSide` when the camera comes within `uDispScale` + 6 (~106 units) of the surface (the v44.21 self-occlude block, `dm.material.side`), and in the 48.13 test that variant linked COLD in play - the watcher's `water [FORK: flags]` x2 is the doubleSided bit (key flags `1027` against the warm `3`). Probably the first low pass over any flooded cavern; **baselined on The Nexus and fixed in v48.15 (below).**

### v48.14 - the Mega Laser that outlived its round, and the replay that never had it

Owner: *"vortex mega laser doesn't clear properly after a match... final kill with mega laser, and the mega laser drawing stayed on after the match, and then didn't re-animate for the replay, the ship just lined up with the old mega laser that was stuck static drawn from just before the round ended"*.

**Jump:** `function _vortexCoreBeamOff` · `player._vcbTTL` (the Mega Laser block of updateAbilities + the backstop at the top of updateWorldEffects) · the core shutdown at the end of `_rplKcStart` · `function _rplBeamSample` / `function _rplBeamAt` / `function _rplActorMesh` · `case 'vortex_core_beam':` in `_rplWfxBuild` and `_rplWfxDress` · `const _RPL_KC_WFX` · the `'cf'` tap (`_spawnClassFireBurst`) in `_rplInstallTaps`

- **⭐⭐ THE BEAM WAS NEVER AN EFFECT.** The pilot's Mega Laser is persistent scene meshes - the stem `player._vortexCoreBeam`, two arm cones, three glow cards - that ONLY updateAbilities poses, and only updateAbilities hides (its "not firing" branch). gameLoop runs nothing of the pilot's while the final kill cam is up (`if (_RPL.kc) {}` - v47.97), so a beam live at the whistle stood frozen for the whole kill cam, and the replayed hull flew back into the spot it was drawn from. Fixed three ways: `_vortexCoreBeamOff()` is the one teardown (death used to clear the stem and arms but not the glow cards, which hung in the air through the ghost cam); `_rplKcStart` ENDS the core (coreActive / coreTimer, as death does) - hiding the meshes is not enough, updateAbilities comes back the moment the kill cam ends or is skipped and would draw the rest of a 4 s core into the round end - and expires the live `_beamFlame` / `_muzzleFlame` fire; and a `_vcbTTL` backstop in updateWorldEffects (fed 0.2 s by every frame that draws the beam), the same shape as the Blaster charge glow's `_bcgTTL`, for the next branch that stops the tick. The console's dev studio hides the meshes too (the paused match does not run updateAbilities).
- **⭐⭐ AND NO REPLAY HAD EVER SEEN IT.** The peer's beam is a world effect (recorded since v48.06), a bot's is 20 Hz tracers (tapped), but the pilot's was neither. `_rplBeamSample` (called from `_rplSample` beside the pose) records one `vortex_core_beam` entry per firing in `R.wf` with a 20 Hz track `bt` (stride 9: t, stem start xyz, direction xyz, length, arms) in the HULL'S OWN FRAME - both the hull and the beam interpolate between the same samples, so the replayed beam can never drift off the ship. The arms are not recorded: they run from the joint to the gun markers the replayed hull carries itself (`m.userData.muzzleNodes`). Rebuilt with updateAbilities' own geometry singletons, 'core_beam' preset, uniforms and the shared glow card material, dressed with its formulas. Serialized (`bt` in `worldFx`), so saved and exported rounds carry it.
- **THE KILL CAM DRAWS BEAMS FROM THE RECORDING.** It borrows the live world, so the live traps, walls and gas still stand in it as they are; but a beam rides a caster who is being replayed, so `_rplWfxReplay` takes an `only` filter and the kill cam rebuilds `_RPL_KC_WFX` (the pilot's beam and the peer's). The live peer beam is hidden while `_RPL.kc` is up - it took `np.position` (live) with `np.mesh.quaternion` (re-posed to the replay), so it would have drawn from where the pilot is along where they faced then.
- **THE PURPLE FIRE COMES BACK TOO.** `_spawnClassFireBurst` is tapped ('cf'; outermost calls only, so muzzle fire lit by emitChassisMuzzleFlash is not doubled - it replays through 'mf'). Every live caller sets `_grow` after the call returns (1.0-1.3), which a tap cannot see, so a lifted 'cf' cloud gets 1.2 rather than the explosion default 2.2.
- **⚠ Teardown:** the arm cone and glow card geometries are module singletons NOT on `_isSharedEffectGeometry`'s list - keepGeo outright; the 'core_beam' materials are RETAINED (a theater match may never have drawn a live beam, and then the replay's are the only holders). The replay's peer-beam material used to be disposed outright; it is retained now as well.
- **MEASURED (Vortex solo on The Nexus, the last Tracker pinned in the beam):** core on at 0.35 s, the Tracker died at 1.01 s (live beam still on - the round end runs abilities until the kill cam), kill cam at 1.25 s: live beam OFF, core ended. The replayed stem + 2 arms + 3 glow cards stood up 4.65 s into the kill cam - exactly where the recording's firing began - and went out 2.85 s later (0.9 s of fight at 1/3). Round 4 then reloaded from IndexedDB into the theater: the beam stands 18.9-19.6 s, absent at 18.7 and from 19.85 (the kill at 19.5, the kill cam took it at ~19.75), 14 fire clouds grew along it at 0.25x, 6 build/teardown seek cycles left programs 176 / geometries 1011 / textures 74 unchanged, zero cold links.
- **⚠ Testing it:** a pane tab that is not in front can be `document.hidden` - then nothing renders, and `_rplFrame` (the recorder and the kill cam) runs from renderFrame, so no round is recorded at all (the sim still runs on the 30 Hz worker). Front the test tab, or the kill cam never happens. `player.spawnProtection = 120` keeps the pilot alive through a staged fight.
- ~~**Open:** the Laser ABILITY's 0.22 s shot (built inline in activateAbility, `'vortexLaserBeam'` game.effects) still does not replay~~ - **replays since v48.16 (below).**

### v48.15 - the water sheet's other side, warmed

From the v48.13 lead (the open item above). **Jump:** `THE WATER SHEET'S OTHER SIDE` in `_prebakeGpuPrime` · `const _side = (_so && _camClear > _ceil + 6.0)` (the v44.21 self-occlude block that flips it)

- **⭐ BASELINED FIRST, ON AN ORDINARY CAVERN.** Solo on The Nexus (`hourglass`, rocky, flooded at -420.8), pilot held 8 u over a basin with the chase eye 50 u above the surface: the displaced sheet went `side` 2 and the watcher logged `water [FORK: flags]` in play - so it is general cavern water, not something the Broken Simulation flooding brought. Decoding `renderer.info.programs`: the sheet (shader lead 57|58) had 164 FrontSide into `postFX.rtScene` (warm - the prime draws it from the spawn), 188 FrontSide into the canvas (srgb, tone-mapped: a warm that compiled against the canvas), and the cold one, 200 - DoubleSide into `postFX.rtScene`, differing from 164 in the doubleSided bit ALONE. The flat Reflector (lead 40|41) is always DoubleSide and was warm.
- **⚠ The Diamond's SECOND cold link (t=52 in the 48.13 test) was mine:** my capture renders went straight to the canvas (`renderer.render(scene, camera)`, no target) from 90-120 u over the water, which built the canvas-target DoubleSide variant. Real play needs one program, not two. A capture that renders to the canvas is its own program family - do not read its links as the game's.
- **THE FIX:** the prime renders from the spawn, far above the water, so they only ever built the side the sheet had then. `_prebakeGpuPrime` now gets the sheet the way the first frame's water update does (`_swBuildHubWaterDispGet` at the Reflector's WL), flips it to its OTHER side, `_warmDrawRoot`s it into `postFX.rtScene` (compile AND draw - ANGLE builds per input layout at the first draw) and puts the side back; the per-frame block owns it from there. Same gate as that block (`window.__waterDisp`, not `_cavernWaterCheap` - the phone / headset water never draws this sheet), before the prime's link drain, and the swap stage runs the prime too.
- **MEASURED (48.15, the same pass):** eye 50 u over the water, sheet `side` 2, `__coldSeen` EMPTY for the whole match; the DoubleSide program (191, flags 1027) exists before play - linked behind the loading overlay.

### v48.16 - the Laser ability in the replay

Owner: *"make the laser ability show in replays too"*.

**Jump:** `function _spawnVortexLaserShot` / `function _spawnVortexLaserPeerBeam` (beside `_vortexCoreBeamOff`) · their call in the `'Laser'` arm of executeAbility and in the `vortex_laser_beam` branch of the effect_spawn handler · the `'vl'` / `'vp'` taps in `_rplInstallTaps` and cases in `_rplFire`

- **The shot was built inline, so no replay had it.** Its tracer, lightning, hit fire and (v48.14) barrel flames already came back through tapped spawners; the shot itself - the thin `'core_beam'` cylinder with its violet backing core, the two arms back to the guns and the three glow cards - was assembled in executeAbility. It is lifted verbatim into `_spawnVortexLaserShot(origin, dir, range, gunA, gunB, life)`: everything it needs is in its arguments, it touches only the scene and `game.effects`, and the shot is FIXED IN THE WORLD from its spawn (updateEffects' `'vortexLaserBeam'` branch only fades it and retracts it muzzle-first) - so a tapped re-call IS the shot. Damage, the water hook, the net events and the tracer / lightning / flames stay in executeAbility. A peer's shot (the one `'core_beam'` cylinder the `vortex_laser_beam` event draws) is lifted the same way into `_spawnVortexLaserPeerBeam`, its water hook left in the handler (the lake is live; a replay never touches it). A bot's Laser was always tracer streaks - it replayed already.
- **Slow motion for free:** the re-called pieces are ordinary `game.effects` entries, and gameLoop ages those at `dt * _rplTimeK()` - so in the kill cam the shot fades at 1/3, and in the studio at its speed.
- **MEASURED (Vortex solo on The Nexus, the last enemy pinned in the aim and finished by the Laser):** live shot 6 pieces (beam + 2 arms + 3 glow cards) at 0.53 s; kill cam at 0.78 s, the live pieces cleared with it (`_rplClearFx`); the REPLAYED shot's 6 pieces appeared at 7.41 s - where the kill cam reaches the kill - and faded out at 8.05 s, 0.65 s of screen for a 0.22 s shot at 1/3. The dev studio, played through the shot at 0.1x and paused: all 6 standing on the replayed Vortex. Console clean, zero cold links.
- **⚠ Staging it:** bots come out of each round start with `spawnProtection` (3), and `takeDamage` returns 0 while it holds - a staged kill in the first seconds of a round silently does nothing. Wait it out. `shipState` reads `'spawning'` for as long as the pilot's own protection is held up (the test's `spawnProtection = 300` loop) - it does not block abilities or the core.

### v48.17 - the damage states in the replay

Owner: *"does the replay show damage states? like the sparking and on fire?"* - then *"sounds good"* to the fix, and watching it: *"can see the ship state in the replay, good"*.

**Jump:** `function _dmgTierOf` / `function _dmgStateEmit` (split out of `emitDamageState`) · `function _burnSprayEmit` (split out of `_tickFireDOTs`) · `function _rplDmgTick` (beside `_rplStateAt`) · the stage + burn bits in `_rplSample`'s `put` · the `_rplDmgTick` calls in `_rplStudioFrame` and `_rplKcFrame` · `damage:` in `__replay.st()`

- **What a replay used to have.** emitDamageState stands down under the kill cam and the studio (v47.97: the live entities are not where their hulls are being drawn), so a replay only had what the recorder caught of the tapped half: the electric arcs (spawnLightningBolt) and the fire puffs (spawnFXBurst) as loose one-offs FROZEN where they spawned - the fire never streamed off the hull (its `wakeVel` drift and the friendly-red tint are set after the call, where a tap cannot see them) - and nothing of the sparks (the v8 spark pool), the smoke (plain particles) or a Pyro burn (`_tickFireDOTs`' particle spray).
- **Now the STAGE is recorded and the live emitters run on the replayed hull.** `_dmgTierOf(entity)` is the one rule (0 none - whole, or shield up, with the v42.06 shield note moved onto it - then 1 sparking < 100 %, 2 electric < 75 %, 3 smoke < 50 %, 4 fire < 25 %), read by the live emitter AND the recorder, which puts it in the state track's flags (bits 2-4) with BURNING (bit 32: `onFireTimer > 0`). The effects body of emitDamageState is `_dmgStateEmit(entity, tier)` verbatim - `entity` needs only position, velocity, team, chassis.hullLength - and the burn spray is `_burnSprayEmit(center, hullLen, dt)`. `_rplDmgTick` hands them a stand-in built from the recorded pose (velocity from the path 50 ms back, so the flames stream aft), on REPLAY time (a paused studio emits nothing; the kill cam's slow motion slows the cadence), with the recorder shut out (`_RPL.nest`) - the kill cam runs while the round is still being recorded.
- **Not recorded any more:** the live emitter's own arcs and puffs (`_RPL.nest` around `_dmgStateEmit`), so a new recording never draws them twice. Pre-48.17 recordings have no stage bits and keep their recorded arcs/puffs - they replay as before.
- **The burn spray stands down under the kill cam** (it puffed at the burning ship's LIVE position while its hull was being replayed elsewhere - the same reason emitDamageState stands down); the burn damage itself still runs.
- **MEASURED (Vortex solo on The Nexus):** a Tracker held at 15 % hull, shield 0, burning, for 2 s -> the recorded track reads `b1:4+burn` from 3.8 s (`__replay.st().damage`); played in the studio at 1x, drifting fire puffs (`wakeVel` set) climb 4 -> 39 live the moment the playhead enters the stage, with the burn spray around them. In a kill cam of a burning victim, particles around the REPLAYED hull stayed 0 until the replay reached the moment it was set alight, then 8-21 plus a flame puff. No game errors. The owner watched it: "can see the ship state in the replay, good".
- **⚠ Testing:** any key skips the kill cam (`onIn` listens for keydown) - a synthetic ability key sent after it starts ends it. And some live particle's `position` is a plain object, not a Vector3 - a monitor that calls `p.position.distanceTo` throws on every tick until it expires.

- **⛔ DESIGN RULE (owner, after v48.17): the replay recorder stays LOCAL.** Asked whether replays should play through the multiplayer handlers (the Quake / Unreal model - a demo is the recorded network stream, so one path serves both): *"the reason why we don't want to do it that way is to keep the mesh file minimal, containing only the necessary data for a smooth and fair battle... and right now, it's smooth and fair"*. So the P2P mesh carries the gameplay minimum and nothing for the replay's sake, and the recorder captures what it needs on each client (more than the net ever carries: the pilot's own Mega Laser arms and glows, the damage stages). Sharing a PURE SPAWNER between a net handler and a replay tap is fine (`_spawnVortexLaserPeerBeam`); sharing the message path, or adding traffic for replays, is not.
